articles.title: Can This Vermont Company Remake the Electric Aviation Industry?
articles.summary:
How Beta Technologies Is Clearing the Runway for Electric Flight
It aims to lift the industry with its aircraft, motors, batteries, and charging network
In the cockpit of Beta Technologies’ Alia CX300, pilot Chris Caputo steers onto Runway 33 at Patrick Leahy Burlington International Airport in Vermont. Cleared for takeoff, he releases the brakes and nudges the throttle forward.
At the back of the aircraft, the five-blade pusher propeller snaps awake, and the Alia bolts forward. There’s no shriek of a turbofan spooling up, no shudder of a piston engine, and no wait for thrust. Just the low hum of an electric motor and a shove of instant acceleration.
Within a few seconds, we’re at 85 knots (almost 160 kilometers per hour), and Caputo rotates the nose upward. The runway drops abruptly away as we climb. Gaining speed and altitude, we head northwest over Lake Champlain. Through the wraparound canopy, I watch the hunched shoulders of Vermont’s Green Mountains shrink under the right wing, with New York’s taller Adirondacks to the left.
Caputo, a former Air Force fighter pilot, flicks the control stick hard left, then right. Despite its 15-meter wingspan, the Alia feels snappy, its fly-by-wire system automatically coordinating aileron and rudder inputs. The machine, he says, is much simpler to manage than the Cessna 182 I flew around Australia in my student-pilot days.

articles.title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
articles.summary:
Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
Welcome to the 26th edition of Cloudflare's DDoS Threat Report. This edition covers the third quarter of 2026 — July, August, and September — and returns the series to its quarterly cadence following the combined H1 2026 volume. The analysis is produced by Cloudforce One, Cloudflare's Threat Intelligence organization, providing a comprehensive analysis of the evolving threat landscape of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks based on data from the Cloudflare network.
Key insights
- Short-burst, low-bandwidth attacks lasting under 10 minutes and 1 Gbps surged by 208%. Conversely, hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps plummeted by nearly 69% from Q2, possibly a reflection of law enforcement actions against four major Internet of Things (IoT) botnets earlier in the year. However, variants continue to emerge, proving that IoT botnets remain a durable, high-volume threat to network infrastructure.
- Threat actors dramatically shifted their reflection and amplification tactics, abruptly abandoning CLDAP floods, which collapsed by 99.5% quarter-over-quarter. Instead, attackers pivoted heavily toward other connectionless protocols, driving a 215% surge in DNS amplification and a 122% increase in general UDP floods.
- Attack targets broadened significantly across both industries and geographies, with the United States reclaiming the most-attacked position from China. Canada and Israel experienced sharp spikes …

articles.title: Vazamento de 40 mil dados do DHS atinge o ICE e a defesa dos EUA

Os arquivos também revelam grupos de permissões que controlam o acesso a sistemas internos. Alguns fazem referência a programas de interceptação de comunicações e operações disfarçadas. articles.title: GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack
articles.summary:
Our jobs as developers are changing. In a couple of years, we’ve gone from writing every line of code to working with AI assistants to orchestrating fleets of agents. But the goal hasn’t changed: ship completed software work. A feature, a bug fix, a security fix. Completed work, not more code, is the output that matters.
Today at GitHub Universe, we shared our vision for GitHub as the most comprehensive software delivery system in the world. We introduced products that bring that vision to life and showed how we’re rebuilding the infrastructure underneath it.
Our vision: From idea to completed software
The SDLC is no longer a linear path from planning to coding to testing to deployment. A code change, a request from a colleague, or a production metric can trigger work anywhere in the system. Most of us (and our agents) jump between different stages, depending on the task at hand. Developers set the direction, make decisions, and stay accountable for what ships. Agents implement and verify changes. And everything feeds into and out of a continuous learning machine that makes the next cycle better.
This agentic software delivery system solves for three things:
Velocity: get from idea to completed software as quickly, efficiently, and cost-effectively as possible
Intelligence: combine context across the platform with a continuous learning engine, so the system gets better as you use it
Quality: make completed work secure by default and catch bugs before they ship

articles.title: “Trabajar tres días a la semana y mantener a la familia”: el pronóstico de Jeff Bezos sobre la IA

Jeff Bezos sostiene que la inteligencia artificial podría permitir que parte de la población trabaje tres días a la semana y mantenga a su familia gracias al aumento de productividad. El fundador de Amazon plantea un escenario en el que la automatización no obligaría a competir con las máquinas mediante jornadas más largas, sino que abriría la posibilidad de producir más con menos esfuerzo humano.
La previsión importa porque el avance de la IA mantiene abierto el debate sobre el futuro del empleo. Mientras algunas voces alertan sobre la pérdida de puestos en actividades administrativas y físicas, Bezos considera que el efecto principal podría ser una reducción del tiempo necesario para generar ingresos suficientes.
Bezos vincula la productividad con jornadas más cortas
Durante una entrevista con Bret Baier en Fox News, Jeff Bezos explicó que algunas personas podrían decidir que ya no necesitan trabajar cinco días a la semana. “Algunas personas también decidirán: ‘¿Sabes qué? Puedo mantener a mi familia trabajando tres días a la semana’”, afirmó.
Para el empresario, esa posibilidad representa el sentido económico de una mayor productividad. Si las herramientas de IA permiten producir más bienes y servicios con una menor cantidad de trabajo, parte de la población podría optar por dedicar más tiempo a otras actividades.

articles.title: Why Africa needs its own AI off switch
articles.summary:
Imagine that it is 6 a.m. in the wholesale markets of Nairobi. Merchants are delivering vegetables from up-country farms to the retailers who sell to the city’s households. Everyone is using M-Pesa, Safaricom’s mobile money platform, when suddenly, the system crashes, bringing the market to a standstill. Imagine that across the continent in Accra, MTN’s MoMo has also crashed, and business in Makola Market has all but stopped.
With the growing number of cyberattacks caused by artificial intelligence, these are highly plausible scenarios. In both these cases, Safaricom, MTN, and the Kenyan and Ghanaian governments need an off switch, or the technical ability and know-how to stop a rogue AI agent from executing its code on their payment systems.
Currently, the conversation on AI agents revolves around China versus the U.S., open versus closed models, and who will dominate the AI race. But in Africa’s capitals, the distinction that will ultimately matter is not whose product was used to build a system, or who dominates whom, but rather whether AI can serve its purpose and be controlled locally. So how can Africa build with agency, and with control over the code and makeup of its own systems, even though they are built on foreign technology?
African countries are already building AI for digital transformation, as outlined in the African Union’s continental AI strategy and country-specific AI strategies. Policymakers are building AI infrastructure but rarely discuss how AI delivers…

Former Yahoo CEO and early Google engineer Marissa Mayer is catching a lot of flak for how she uses AI. In an interview about her new app Dazzle, an AI assistant that learns from your camera roll, Mayer poses what she believes is an impressive flex for the product: It helped her come up with three bullet points about her 10-year-old daughter for a birthday presentation at school, describing her as “empathetic, creative, and an animal lover.”
It’s a vague description, like a generic horoscope — it could probably describe a lot of 10-year-olds.
Some onlookers, like progressive activist Leah Greenberg, marveled that “the fact that Marissa Mayer would voluntarily disclose this to a reporter is a pretty good demonstration of how deeply the culture of Silicon Valley has diverged from the rest of humanity.”
Perhaps Mayer drew so much backlash because we have repeatedly observed sheltered billionaires suggest that we outsource child-rearing — one of life’s greatest tests of patience, humility, and kindness — to a computer that is incapable of understanding human emotion.

articles.title: Ukrainian Hive and Nefilim Ransomware Affiliate Gets 70 Months in US Prison
articles.summary:
A 36-year-old Ukrainian national was sentenced to prison in the US for his role in Nefilim ransomware attacks.
The man, Artem Aleksandrovych Stryzhak, who had been living in Barcelona, was arrested in Spain in June 2024 and extradited to the US in April 2025. He pleaded guilty in December 2025.
According to court documents, Stryzhak joined the Nefilim ransomware operation as an affiliate in June 2021 and used the malware in attacks against organizations in the US and abroad.
Stryzhak agreed with Nefilim administrator Volodymyr Tymoshchuk to pay the Nefilim administrators 20% of the ransom proceeds extorted from victims.
The defendant operated as a Nefilim ransomware affiliate between June 2021 and October 2021. One of his victims was an unnamed company in the oil and gas transportation industry.
Documents presented in court also show that Stryzhak was one of the early affiliates to join the Hive ransomware group, which hit over 1,500 victims worldwide between June 2021 and January 2023.
The documents show that Stryzhak used the Hive ransomware against seven victim organizations, including a dental office, a healthcare provider, and law firms. Some of the victims paid a ransom, and the cybercriminals provided a decryption key to recover the encrypted files.
Stryzhak was sentenced to 70 months in prison for conspiracy to commit computer fraud.

articles.title: Systems Thinking Is Vital in the Age of AI
articles.summary:
Modern engineering projects increasingly combine human judgment with machine capability. An engineer can define a problem, then ask an artificial intelligence tool to search relevant research and technical standards, generate design options, test them in simulation, and compare the results. The engineer can then bring the results to specialists who understand the parts AI cannot judge on its own, such as whether a design can be built safely, whether it makes sense in a particular setting, or how it might affect its users. The final decision about whether and how to move forward remains a human responsibility.
AI can help engineers do early project steps that once required several people with different technical skills. The engineer’s role is therefore expanding from performing each technical step to deciding how people, machines, and specialists’ knowledge should work together on the project.
The problem, not the title
Engineering has always been divided into disciplines, and for good reasons. Electrical, mechanical, civil, software, and other engineering fields require deep knowledge that takes years to develop. AI does not replace that need. It simply changes how easily engineers can explore the parts of a problem that sit outside their own specialty.
Consider a software engineer working on a medical device. AI can help the engineer review relevant biomedical research, understand unfamiliar terms, analyze data, and build an early model.

articles.title: Circuit Mind lands $25M and puts AI agents to work checking circuit board schematics - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Circuit Mind lands $25M and puts AI agents to work checking circuit board schematics
British circuit board design startup Circuit Mind Ltd. today announced it has raised $25 million in new funding to extend its artificial intelligence platform across more of the hardware design process.
A verification tool that puts AI agents to work hunting for errors in schematics launched at the same time.
Circuit Mind offers software that automates much of the manual work behind printed circuit board design. Engineers can spend more than a year on a new piece of hardware, according to the company, some of it reading datasheets that run to thousands of pages. Mistakes often stay hidden until a prototype is physically built and tested.
In the company’s view, general-purpose large language models are not up to the task on their own, since they have never been trained on professionally designed circuits. Circuit Mind’s platform layers AI agents over a patented, physics-based engine that tests each design decision against electrical limits.

Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. Enterprise artificial intelligence context startup Jedify Inc. today formally launched Data Agents, a product that lets business teams set up autonomous AI analysts by describing the work they want done in plain language.
Data Agents takes on a longstanding limit of business intelligence software, where analysts have to build dashboards ahead of time around the questions they expect people to ask. Generic AI assistants have tried to fill that gap. In Jedify’s telling, those tools end up guessing at what a business means from its raw tables and schemas.
The company’s core product is a context graph that pulls structured data and documents into a single model of how a business works, down to metric definitions and record-level permissions. Data Agents runs on top of it. Because joins and schema mapping are already worked out inside the graph, building an agent comes down to describing the question.
Users decide when an agent runs, whether on request, on a schedule or when a condition they have defined is met. A market that starts to underperform is the kind of anomaly an agent is meant to catch on its own, and Jedify’s deep research engine then works out what most likely drove the change.

articles.title: Cómo saber qué aplicaciones usan el micrófono del celular y bloquear los permisos que no necesitan

Revisar qué aplicaciones usan el micrófono del celular y bloquear los permisos innecesarios permite reducir el riesgo que datos, conversaciones o hábitos de uso queden expuestos. Los teléfonos actuales muestran señales cuando una app activa este sensor, pero la protección depende también de que cada usuario revise con frecuencia las autorizaciones concedidas.

For companies operating in ride-hailing, delivery services, and electric mobility sectors, getting a product into users’ hands is only one part of the challenge.

Dabei kamen sie allein für die Jahre 2022 bis 2024 auf 413 dokumentierte Sicherheitslücken. Persönliche Daten
Aus diesen Daten lassen sich mitunter viele persönliche Informationen auslesen – etwa Wohnort, Arbeitsplatz, Hobbys oder die Schule der Kinder. So geschehen beispielsweise im Jahr 2024 bei Volkswagen.

HyperFlow and Third-Generation HyperFlex
A major new feature of the Agilex 27 family is HyperFlow. HyperFlow is a new full-chip distributed data network that Altera says can move data at multi-terabit-per-second rates throughout the FPGA. That traffic runs on a dedicated network instead of the programmable fabric, so it does not consume soft logic resources or add routing congestion. That leaves more FPGA resources for the application. As an example, a 1.6TbE Ethernet port can bring traffic in through hardened I/O, HyperFlow can carry it across the chip, and the soft logic can spend its resources on processing rather than moving data.

articles.title: CISA warns of hackers now exploiting critical Node2Shell flaw
articles.summary:
On Tuesday, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirmed that hackers have begun exploiting a critical Brotli vulnerability known as Node2Shell, Broccoli2Shell, and HTTP2Shell.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497, this critical-severity flaw stems from an out-of-bounds write weakness in the Brotli decoder used to expand data compressed with Google's widely popular Brotli lossless compression algorithm.
Unprivileged attackers can use a maliciously crafted Brotli-compressed stream to trigger crashes or memory leaks and, in some cases, gain remote code execution on devices with vulnerable Brotli libraries or binaries.
The security issue was first identified in the Node.js JavaScript runtime environment, but it also affects HTTP servers and clients that rely on vulnerable Brotli implementations.
On Sunday, Microsoft also pushed an emergency .NET security update, warning that attackers could exploit it to escalate privileges on systems with a vulnerable .NET version.
CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday and ordered US government agencies to patch their systems within two weeks, by November 10, as mandated by its Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.

Physics-based analysis becomes more consequential as chips, packages, boards, and systems are designed together.
Every hardware design contains decisions made before the team fully understands their physical consequences. An architecture is chosen. Components are placed. Materials are selected. Engineers bring experience and judgment to those choices, but the detailed physics often arrives later, when changing course is harder and more expensive.
That order of work limits what engineers can build. When every answer requires substantial preparation, compute and specialist time, teams have to decide which questions are worth asking. Promising ideas can be set aside because there is no practical way to investigate them within the schedule.
We built Vinci to change that. We recently announced a $250 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation. The investment gives us the resources to accelerate a goal that reaches well beyond any single analysis: shortening the distance between what engineers can imagine and what they can build.
The cost of slow analysis extends into decisions made long before a simulation begins. Teams simplify designs so they can evaluate them. They add margin where uncertainty remains. They carry assumptions forward because testing every alternative would take too long.

articles.summary:
Cloudflare recently made Quicksilver available to customers for the first time, as a new mode for Workers KV called KV Instant. Reads resolve in 1.62 ms at the 99th percentile, compared with 287 ms for classic KV. What determines whether a team can use it isn't the latency, but the envelope around it.
Quicksilver is Cloudflare’s own configuration store, introduced in 2020. Nearly every request to Cloudflare looks up at least one key in it, Rob Sutter writes, and it has never been a customer-facing product. Brendan Irvine-Broque, who works on Cloudflare’s developer platform, announced the change on X:
we have this crazy key-value store at Cloudflare called Quicksilver
instantly updates keys across our whole network. microsecond reads from every location. stupid fast
our customers have asked us for years to make it available
we finally did – in a way we think is quite simple - as a new mode for Workers KV
The published figures, measured to over 300 edge locations:
| Mode | p99 reads (all) | median write replication | p99 write replication | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Instant | 1.62 ms | 107 ms | 256 ms | 
| Classic | 287 ms | under 1 s | 4.38 s | 
Cloudflare notes it has no sub-second fidelity for replication lag in classic mode, so the classic median and p95 figures are upper bounds rather than measurements. p95 reads in Instant mode are reported in microseconds.

Discovered in a core component of EBS's Application Object Library and tracked as CVE-2026-101767, this flaw lets unauthenticated threat actors with HTTP network access take over vulnerable systems in low-complexity attacks.
Oracle released security updates to address the issue in its October 2026 Critical Security Patch Update on October 20 and urged customers to patch their systems immediately.
"In some instances, it has been reported that attackers have been successful because targeted customers had failed to apply available Oracle patches," it said. "Oracle therefore strongly recommends that customers remain on actively-supported versions and apply security patches without delay."
While Oracle has not yet tagged CVE-2026-101767 as exploited in the wild, threat intelligence company Defused said on Tuesday that it already spotted threat actors scanning the Internet for vulnerable systems.
"Our Oracle E-Business Suite decoys recorded exploratory exploits against CVE-2026-101767, an unauthenticated SQL injection in EBS's Thin Client Framework servlet that chains to remote code execution, this morning, Oct 27," Defused warned.

Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
Living digital twins are helping industrial plants run more like living systems, and setting the stage for industries that work in sync.
Most people associate industrial environments with cold steel and clockwork machinery. Functionally, though, a plant or factory is more like a living thing: It has a pulse, even a metabolism. It goes through wear and tear as it ages, and signs of deteriorating health often show up as barely perceptible irregularities.
Digital twin technology has long aimed to mirror that dynamism and model anomalies that may be symptomatic of larger problems. But earlier implementations were a few beats behind physical reality; they were incapable of real-time analysis and unable to proactively address any issues detected. They focused more on simulation, observation and what-if scenario planning, rather than closed-loop execution. Rather than serving as a digital mirror of reality that can spot anomalies or suggest optimizations, a living digital twin combines a dynamic, high-fidelity digital representation of complex operations with the capacity to intervene in the physical world through operations and control systems.
AI is at the center of this change. Rob McGreevy, chief product officer at AVEVA, likens newer, AI-infused digital twins to organisms that grow and evolve. These “living” versions are adaptive, evergreen models of a plant’s assets and processes. Because they keep pace …

articles.title: A hidden ocean change near Antarctica could have global consequences
articles.summary:
The rapid decline of Antarctic sea ice since 2016 has triggered a dramatic shift in a crucial part of Earth’s climate system, scientists say.
In a paper published Wednesday, researchers documented a sharp salinity increase in a vast layer of the Southern Ocean, extending from 2,300 to 4,000 feet deep and encircling Antarctica. The shift reverses decades of freshening and echoes ocean changes usually associated with major global climate shifts over millennia but is now happening in just a few years.
The switch from a decades-long trend of freshening water to increasing salinity has implications that could extend beyond Antarctica. The layer, known as Antarctic Intermediate Water, spreads northward into the Indian, Pacific, and Atlantic oceans, transporting heat, carbon, oxygen, and nutrients toward the tropics, and even across the equator, said co-author Bishakhdatta Gayen, a researcher and professor at the University of Melbourne and at the Centre for Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences in Bengaluru, India.
Gayen said the study combined six independent datasets to track changes in the Southern Ocean from 2004 to 2024. The data came from Argo floats, which drift through the ocean and periodically descend to different depths to measure water properties such as density and salinity, then resurface to transmit the readings. A 2025 study also detected increasing surface salinity linked to declining sea ice, he added.

articles.title: Building an Offline-First AI Coding Tutor for Low-End Android Phones
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- On low-end devices in low-bandwidth markets, a full storage volume is a normal operating condition rather than an edge case, so any await on a cache or database write inside a critical render path is a latent blank screen and should be treated as a non-fatal degradation instead.
- localStorage is the wrong persistence layer for any cache that scales with content or locale, because its roughly 5MB ceiling and synchronous API impose the heaviest cost on precisely the underpowered devices you are trying to serve, while IndexedDB with a dual-read migration window lets you move without stranding existing users.
- WebAssembly runtimes such as Pyodide and sql.js make server-free code execution viable on smartphones, but only if you defer initialisation into a Web Worker and treat cold-start cost as a first-class UX problem rather than a benchmark footnote.
- AI features that depend on a hosted endpoint should be designed with an explicit degradation contract, which includes a defined second tier, a defined timeout, persisted session state across the switch, and feedback formats that stay useful when the weaker model answers.
- Discoverability and usability are different properties, and a feature placed outside a user's working line of sight is functionally a feature that does not exist.

Sykophantie = Anbiederung der KI

Enterprises should rethink this idea. Security teams cannot patch at machine speed, but they can reduce what an attacker can reach after exploitation by focusing on identity as the control plane.
Beyond the initial exploitation, the ultimate incident severity depends heavily on which service accounts, API keys, cloud roles, and tokens the compromised workload can use and what they can access.

Separate false failures caused by voltage droop from real structural defects.
By Aakash Jani, Henrique Mendes, and Robert Wilcox
In a previous blog, we highlighted the importance of combining physical and functional sensors to plan for new workloads. This use case remains relevant for high-performance AI and HPC systems because ‘spiky’ workloads induce severe droops that dominate power budgets.
Your $1 billion ASIC just had a scan failure during an In-System Test. How can you tell whether the failure is an actual structural failure, or one caused by physical phenomena like voltage droop? Scan patterns can often generate intense switching activity when long or multiple chains are toggled, which may induce a voltage droop. If the failure is due to a voltage droop, you have a few options: slow the shift clock, raise the voltage, or repartition your scan patterns. Without physical sensors that report conditions during the test, teams can’t tell the two cases apart and might throw away good parts on false failures.
Co-mingling physical and functional sensors is necessary across the system lifecycle because functional and physical failures are connected. Let’s move further down the system lifecycle into silicon deployment for another example.

articles.title: Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot
articles.summary:
Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot
A powerful feedback loop could drive more warming than predicted.
Climate change itself is increasingly fueling climate change. Rising concentrations of greenhouse gases are driving up global temperatures, setting off dangerous feedback loops that we have not fully accounted for in our climate models—or our emissions-reduction goals.
Scientists have long warned that warming would propel further warming in various ways, but a growing number of observations and studies are at last providing a sharper sense of just how powerful these cascading effects could be. And, by extension, they’re showing how much faster the planet may warm in this century.
A study in Environmental Research Letters in September, synthesizing the results of previous papers, found that the additional carbon dioxide and methane released from thawing permafrost, intensifying wildfires, hotter lakes and reservoirs, and wetter, warmer wetlands alone could drive global average temperatures up 0.2 °C to 0.4 °C this century. That would come on top of the 2.6°C of warming above preindustrial levels that modelers are already expecting through 2100. The additional heat could subject many of the world’s cities to monthslong heat waves and expose hundreds of millions of people to flooding.

Artificial Intelligence
Distributed training with Ray Train DLCs and EFA on EKS
What usually stops PyTorch training from scaling out to a cluster is the container, not the model code. Every container needs the same CUDA runtime, a PyTorch build compiled against it, NCCL (NVIDIA Collective Communications Library), the Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) userspace libraries, the AWS OFI NCCL plugin that connects NCCL to EFA, and a Ray version the cluster operator agrees with. Building that image and rebuilding it each time one of those pieces moves is a project of its own, and it has nothing to do with the model you set out to train. The Ray Train Deep Learning Container (DLC) is that image, built by AWS. AWS assembles the stack, tests it as one unit, publishes it in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) Public and keeps it patched.
Ray runs a job across machines as a single cluster with two roles. The Ray head coordinates and runs the global control store that tracks cluster state, the dashboard and job server you submit jobs to. Ray worker nodes supply the GPUs and run the training processes. Each worker joins the cluster by connecting to the head’s address when it starts. On Kubernetes, each of these is a pod. Kubernetes has no built-in idea of a Ray cluster, so something must create the head and worker pods, start Ray in the right role in each, point the workers at the head, and replace pods that fail. articles.title: AI agents need to be replaceable – without losing your work
articles.summary:
AI agents need to be replaceable – without losing your work
An agent receives approval to process a partial refund. It sends the request to a payment API, and the process crashes. Maybe the payment service completed the refund. Maybe the request never went through. A replacement agent spins up and finds an operation record marked dispatched with no outcome written.
This kind of ambiguity isn’t unique to agents. Any distributed worker crashing mid-mutation faces the same problem. But a conventional worker resumes a predetermined workflow from the last checkpoint. An agent does something more dangerous: it reasons on its own. Given the same customer request and no outcome record, it might come up with a different plan, pick different parameters, or decide to issue a new refund instead of continuing the one already approved.
“An agent does something more dangerous: it reasons on its own.”
If the original refund went through, a second attempt refunds the customer twice. The charge still has enough remaining balance to cover another partial refund, so nothing stops it.
The replacement must inherit the original operation, not reinterpret it.
The operation must outlive the agent
An agent’s process, its in-memory variables, its transient reasoning context: all disposable. The business operation is not. The refund, its approval, its parameters, its current status. We urgently need to monitor AI agents’ actions in real time
Right now, we’re effectively flying blind when deploying these tools. Here’s what we need to do instead.
This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about how they’d be graded. Around the same time, another OpenAI agent accessed private files from an Australian government website. It’s a problem that’s by no means confined to OpenAI. In the months since, Anthropic, Google, and Meta have also disclosed incidents in which their agents have gone off track. And worryingly, in many cases the agents eluded the very researchers and safety teams tasked with monitoring them.
AI agents are taking unauthorized actions, and the companies building and running them are mostly relying on luck and hindsight to mitigate any harmful impacts. They must do more to ensure safety. That’s why EU regulators and US agencies are rightfully calling for agent developers and deployers to monitor agents in real time. But these rules assume that companies can see what their agents are doing and why—when in reality, they lack sufficient visibility.

articles.title: Chrome Opens Trial for the Email Verification API: Letting Sites Verify Without Sending Emails
articles.summary:
Google has opened a Chrome origin trial for the Email Verification API, a WICG proposal that lets a browser confirm a visitor owns the email address they typed, without sending a single message. The trial began in Chrome 150 on desktop, with Gmail taking part as the first participating provider.
The idea replaces the familiar one-time code or magic link. Today a user enters an email, leaves for their inbox, copies a code, and returns, a context switch that often loses them. The proposal uses a three-party model where the browser sits between the site (the "verifier") and the mailbox provider (the "issuer"). If the user is already signed in to their provider, the browser quietly fetches a signed token and drops it into the form, and the server validates that token on submission. Google notes the issuer never learns which site made the request.
For developers the front end implementation is fairly straightforward. The email field needs an autocomplete hint, plus a hidden input carrying a session-bound nonce:
<input id="email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email">
<input type="hidden" name="token" nonce={nonce} autocomplete="email-verification-token">
The heavier work sits on the server side, where the token's signature is checked against the provider's keys. Resend's Phil Nash, who wrote a walkthrough of the flow, published an npm package and a Next.js example to handle that parsing and validation.

For a Platform team that wants to support many agentic use cases, that’s a platform product to design and operate. articles.title: What happens when the agent is long gone, but its access key lives on?
articles.summary:
What happens when the agent is long gone, but its access key lives on?
Imagine: There’s a line on the credential report that no one on the platform team can explain. An IAM user called research-agent-2 has an access key created 14 months ago that was last used 11 months ago. And it’s still active.
The project it supported closed long ago, and the person who approved it doesn’t even work at the company anymore.
While this example is hypothetical, the lifecycle problem isn’t.
This doesn’t require carelessness. An agent is created for a task, the task ends, and nobody revisits its access. A departing person triggers offboarding; a finished agent just leaves a closed tab. AWS IAM user access keys don’t expire automatically, so a forgotten key stays valid until somebody disables or deletes it.
“A departing person triggers offboarding; a finished agent just leaves a closed tab.”
OWASP puts improper offboarding first in its 2025 Top 10 for non-human identities, and the remedy reads like this series’ premise: retire what’s no longer needed, and give the rest an accountable owner. The hard part is knowing what exists.
The problem is that attackers move faster than an annual audit ever could. articles.title: Physics-Based Validation: The Foundation Of Trustworthy Agentic EDA
articles.summary:
What self-verifying agents validate their decisions against and why physics-based engines are the authority on correctness.
This is the third article in a series examining what it takes to build production-ready AI agents for EDA. The first explored the architectural decisions required for agents to operate reliably in production environments. The second examined what self-verifying means in an agentic EDA workflow: how agents continuously check their decisions as they work, rather than waiting until the end of a run.
But what exactly are those decisions being verified against?
The answer is physics. More specifically, the deterministic, physics-based EDA engines that define whether a design is correct. A self-verifying agent checks its own work, and a physics-validated workflow confirms that work is correct.
Chip design has always faced physics-based constraints. Every transistor, every wire, every timing path, and every thermal gradient is governed by the fixed laws of physics, regardless of how the design was created. This is why tapeout is binary: silicon either works or it does not.
When AI enters this domain, that physical reality does not change. The relevant question is not whether an AI system can reason about physics, but whether the outputs it produces have been confirmed by the engines that enforce that physics.
That distinction separates a model that is capable of reasoning about physics from a workflow that is physics-validated.

articles.title: Nvidia launches a promptable transcription model
articles.summary:
Nvidia launches a promptable transcription model
Nvidia on Wednesday launched Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, its latest multilingual transcription model. The new open-weight model, the company says, ranks first on Hugging Face’s Open ASR open model leaderboard for English, with an average word error rate of 5.33%, and also sits at the top of two speaker-attribution benchmarks.
But what’s maybe even more interesting is that this is a promptable transcription model. Being promptable here means that the user can give the model specific instructions before it listens. Typically, that means setting the context for the transcription by telling the model that a given audio file is a medical discussion in English, for example, and giving it a list of medical terms.
Users can also tell the model to label each speaker or ask it questions about the audio. They can request a verbatim transcript or a cleaned-up version, and tell it how to format numbers, for example.
Nvidia bundles these capabilities, along with translation, into a single checkpoint, which could simplify the work of building applications around them.
Ideally, setting this context reduces the error rate. The trade-off is that these models are much larger than traditional transcription models, which are often under a billion parameters in size. Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is a 30B mixture-of-experts model with 4 billion active parameters.

Voilà une histoire qui devrait rappeler aux utilisateurs d'IA que cet outil doit toujours être utilisé avec parcimonie et méfiance dans bien des domaines. Celui du droit est concerné dans le sujet qui nous intéresse aujourd'hui.

Personally identifiable information belonging to thousands of U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees has been published online after a hacker stole reams of data in a previously undisclosed breach at the government department earlier this year.
The breach includes names, job titles, and work contact information, such as email addresses, cell phone numbers, and office locations, of more than 40,000 people who work for the federal department, including border and immigration agents, cybersecurity staffers, and senior department officials.
A hacker who goes by the handle Department of Peace claimed they obtained the data from an Okta single sign-on system used by Homeland Security to allow employees and contractors across its various agencies to log in to its central network. The Okta system also contains IT and log-in records associated with the employees’ user account, including details about which systems and internal apps they are permitted to access.
More than half of the dataset — some 21,000 records — relate to employees with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), who work at airports and other ports of entry.
The data also contains records associated with another 10,000 employees of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and its Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) unit, and just under a 1,000 employees who work at U.S. cybersecurity defense agency CISA.

articles.title: Unos científicos "culpan" a un virus de colarse en el ADN de los chimpancés e impedirles desarrollar un cerebro humano
articles.summary:
Los chimpancés tienen un parentesco increíble con los humanos. Solo tenemos un 1,2% de ADN diferente. Pero entonces, ¿por qué somos aparentemente tan distintos? Es cierto que los chimpancés son animales muy inteligentes, pero no tanto como los humanos. Nuestro cerebro está más desarrollado, por lo que puede que, hace mucho tiempo, sucediese algo que hiciera divergir el desarrollo de nuestros cerebros . Qué pudo ser eso que tanto nos alejó ha sido una incógnita durante mucho tiempo, pero ahora unos científicos de la Universidad de Lund han dado una posible respuesta: quizás se trató de un virus.
El virus que lo cambió todo. Existen algunos virus que no solo invaden las células ajenas y utilizan su maquinaria para reproducirse. También son capaces de insertar su propio ADN en medio del ADN del huésped. Si esto ocurre en las células germinales, la inserción puede pasar de generación en generación. Por eso, los científicos de la Universidad de Lund examinaron el ADN de chimpancé en busca de fragmentos virales que pudiesen resultar sospechosos. Les llamó especialmente la atención la presencia de ADN de un virus llamado Pan troglodytes endogenous retrovirus-1 (PTERV1), ya que se encuentra en estos y otros simios africanos, pero no en los humanos. Era un gran candidato.

Les entreprises investissent massivement dans l’intelligence artificielle, mais les résultats sont encore bien loin des promesses. Selon Gartner, seules 3% dépassent leurs objectifs d’économies grâce aux gains de productivité. Un constat qui n’empêche pas les budgets de continuer à grimper.
L’intelligence artificielle devait révolutionner la productivité des entreprises et, accessoirement, leur faire économiser beaucoup d’argent. Pour le moment, la seconde partie de la promesse peine sérieusement à se concrétiser. Selon des résultats présentés par Gartner le 26 octobre, seules 3% des organisations parviennent à dépasser leurs objectifs d’économies grâce aux gains de productivité générés par l'IA.
Un résultat particulièrement décevant quand on sait que 77% des membres des conseils d’administration s’attendent justement à ce que cette technologie permette de travailler plus efficacement tout en réduisant les dépenses.
Des budgets qui explosent sans les économies promises
Le plus étonnant est que les entreprises ne semblent pas décidées à lever le pied. Selon Gartner, 85% prévoient d’augmenter leurs dépenses dans l’IA en 2027 alors que 38% dépassent déjà leur budget initial.
Les entreprises continuent donc d’investir tandis que les économies réalisées restent en deçà de leurs attentes. Entre les abonnements aux outils, les infrastructures informatiques et l’adaptation des méthodes de travail, déployer de l’IA coûte encore cher.

articles.title: The GEO Playbook: How Australian brands can optimise for Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT search - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
For more than two decades, the standard playbook for Australian businesses online was straightforward: identify target keywords, optimize metadata, acquire authoritative backlinks, and compete for a spot in Google’s “ten blue links.”
That paradigm has fundamentally fractured.
With the rollout of Google AI Overviews and the rise of conversational answer engines like ChatGPT Search and Perplexity, search engines are shifting from navigational directories to synthesis engines. Instead of presenting users with a list of external destinations to evaluate, large language models (LLMs) parse the web in real time, extract key facts, and deliver direct, conversational answers.
For digital marketers and business leaders across Australia, this shift presents a new challenge: Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO). To remain visible, brands must learn how to earn recommendations and citations directly inside AI-synthesized answers.
What is Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)?
Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) is the practice of structuring, writing, and technically delivering website content so that it can be accurately crawled, ingested, and cited by generative AI engines.
While traditional SEO focuses on maximizing organic rank positions and direct page clicks, GEO focuses on information gain and citation share. It’s structuring and adding information to a webpage that improves the chances that an AI agent selects your brand (or page) as a primary source when answering user queries.

articles.title: Is It Getting Hot In Here? Why Thermal Is No Longer A Signoff Problem
articles.summary:
Applying the appropriate level of simulation and abstraction at each stage of the design process is key to effective thermal analysis.
AI, high-performance computing and advanced semiconductor packaging have pushed power density higher, and that means managing heat is becoming one of the most consequential challenges in electronic design.
The issue is no longer simply how to cool a chip after it has been designed. Thermal behavior now affects decisions spanning device performance, package architecture, mechanical stress, reliability, floor planning and ultimately system performance. So engineering teams must shift thermal analysis to earlier in the design process as they consider a much broader multi-physics strategy.
Traditionally, engineers could isolate and analyze many physical effects separately. Electrical performance could be evaluated in one environment, thermal behavior in another and mechanical stress in another and so on. But with increasing integration, a change intended to improve performance in one domain can create unintended consequences elsewhere. Higher power can increase temperature; temperature can change electrical behavior; and thermal expansion can introduce mechanical stress that ultimately affects reliability.

articles.title: Cadillac Escalade IQ review: Huge battery, huge range, huge SUV
articles.summary:
“Please have at least 125 miles of range left when we pick it up.” That request from the people who look after the Cadillac press cars wasn’t going to be hard to honor. The electric Escalade IQ arrived with an indicated range of 440 miles (708 km), and with a full week of work to squeeze in, getting anywhere close to needing to recharge it seemed unlikely. With more than 200 kWh of lithium-ion battery between its axles, range is one thing the big electric Caddy needn’t worry about.
Designed and debuted during a time of greater EV optimism, the Escalade is Cadillac’s statement that swapping out a V8 for a pair of powerful electric motors is no compromise to its ambitions, even if the brand’s future will now include a mix of electric and combustion cars beyond 2030. It shares a battery pack and much else with other full-size GM EVs we’ve tested: the Chevrolet Silverado EV, the GMC Sierra EV, and of course the divisive Hummer EVs. And like those trucks and SUVs, the Escalade is large and heavy—just small enough to fit into a standard parking space, with a curb weight sufficient to push it into the Class 3 truck category.
So, the side mirrors are flat, and there’s no formal EPA range—Cadillac says it achieves 460 miles (740 km) on the EPA test cycle—but there are plenty of airbags, even though the 9,046 lb (4,103 kg) curb weight does not require them. articles.title: Instagram monetizará videos largos: “exploramos opciones para que los creadores reciban pago”, afirma director de la app
articles.summary:
Adam Mosseri, director de Instagram, reaccionó a los videos de larga duración que la plataforma comenzó a probar y afirmó que exploran opciones de pago para quienes produzcan ese tipo de contenidos.
“Entendemos que la economía es muy importante, y estamos explorando múltiples opciones para ayudar a los creadores de videos de formato largo a recibir pago”, señaló en Threads.
La iniciativa se vincula con Features, la nueva función con la que Instagram permitirá publicar videos horizontales de hasta 90 minutos.
Por ahora, la herramienta está en fase de prueba y solo está disponible para un grupo de creadores de contenido en Estados Unidos. Mosseri advirtió que el despliegue será gradual. “Esto va a tomar tiempo para que esté bien, pero estamos emocionados y comprometidos”, explicó.
Además, indicó que las características todavía no fueron lanzadas por completo y que la compañía amplía lentamente el acceso mientras recopila comentarios.
Cómo funciona el nuevo formato de video en Instagram
Features está diseñada para que los usuarios puedan pasar de clips breves a contenidos extensos sin salir de Instagram.
Los Reels funcionarán como adelantos: si un creador vincula un video corto con una producción completa, quienes encuentren ese fragmento podrán pulsarlo y continuar la reproducción.
El formato apunta a contenidos como entrevistas, episodios de pódcast y videopodcast, que requieren más tiempo de reproducción.

articles.title: Volt Typhoon hides zero-day attacks using 'Silent Train' framework
articles.summary:
Chinese state-sponsored hacking group Volt Typhoon has been using a framework that relies on rotating chains of connected devices compromised on demand, including for zero-day attacks targeting high-value systems.
The framework has been dubbed Silent Train because the threat actor uses it against select targets, cleans it up after each operation, and refreshes it continuously.
Researchers at Black Lotus Labs, the threat research division of communications company Lumen, have been tracking Silent Train for three years and confirmed that Volt Typhoon exploited at least four zero-day vulnerabilities in attacks targeting edge and management infrastructure.
Targets include telecommunication firms, government agencies, defense contractors, educational institutes, utilities/critical infrastructure, satellite service providers, IT firms, MSPs, transportation, aviation, and emergency services.
Black Lotus Labs’ observations indicate the most targeted regions are California, Texas, and Hawaii, suggesting a focus on Indo-Pacific matters.
Volt Typhoon previously targeted U.S. critical infrastructure, including communications, energy, transportation, and water systems, with CISA warning that it seeks to establish access for potential disruption during a future crisis or conflict.
According to the researchers, Silent Train's deployment was partly fueled by the FBI's disruption of KV-Botnet, a botnet that Volt Typhoon used to evade detection when attacking critical infrastructure in the US.…

The group brings African founders and VCs together with three aims – increasing funding into Africa, eliminating bad term sheets, and helping founders build the networks they need.
“For 10 years I’ve watched great African founders struggle to reach the right investors, and sign terms they didn’t need to accept,” said McLeod. “The group showed what happens when founders and investors talk openly. Investable.Africa takes that to every founder on the continent, not just the ones who already have the right phone numbers.”
The platform allows founders to build a profile covering their problem, solution, traction, team and current round, with every profile checked by the Investable.Africa team before going live. SemiAnalysis’ Joey Brookhart helps break down the Anthropic S-1 and why he thinks the company could be worth $10 trillion.
Anthropic just filed its S-1 to go public on the Nasdaq, and it could start trading as soon as next month at a valuation of anywhere between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion. That would immediately make it one of the most valuable companies on the planet.
But the price tag really isn’t the whole story here. The S-1 document published earlier this week is hundreds upon hundreds of pages filled with details that finally paint a picture of the economics of a frontier AI lab. As you might imagine, that picture is both really complicated and built on a series of very, very ambitious assumptions about the future and what AI will do to it.
So I wanted to have Joey on the show to help break down what this document tells us, both about Anthropic’s finances and the broader AI economy. articles.title: GitHub saw 7.4B commits in September, adding 4M CPU cores and 160 PB of storage to keep up
articles.summary:
GitHub saw 7.4B commits in September, adding 4M CPU cores and 160 PB of storage to keep up
GitHub is seeing unprecedented demand and is updating its core infrastructure to keep pace.
In August, GitHub said it was seeing 2.9 billion commits per month, up from 1.4 billion in April. At its GitHub Universe conference on Wednesday, the company announced that it is now seeing 7.4 billion commits per month. To put that into perspective, developers pushed 65 million monthly commits to the platform in 2024.
That kind of growth is a great problem to have, but the company’s outages have become something of a recurring theme. The reason is rapid usage growth, driven mostly by “agentic demand,” as the company puts it.
4 million more CPU cores
In August, GitHub CTO Vlad Fedorov announced that the platform had added 3 million CPU cores — mostly on Azure — to support this growth. Now, GitHub says it has added 4 million CPU cores, plus 160 petabytes of high-speed storage and more compute power for GitHub Actions so far this year
The company also added 50 Tb/s of network capacity to keep all of this data flowing.
A new GitHub architecture is coming
GitHub also used this announcement to reiterate its commitment to rearchitecting its platform to separate compute and storage. It first talked about this earlier this month. At that time, the company noted that its internal benchmarks show that this new architecture can deliver up to 35x higher write throughput, for example.

Why it matters: Plenty of off-the-shelf drones can tail a cyclist down a trail these days, but most of them still lean on GPS to keep track of where they are. That's a problem in a forest, where a thick canopy can make the signal pretty unreliable. A lab at Purdue University has now shown off a drone that chases a person through the woods with no GPS at all.
Purdue computer science professor Aniket Bera posted the 44-second video on LinkedIn last Friday. It shows a quadcopter from his IDEAS Lab weaving between trees to keep a person in frame. And the drone works it all out on its own computer, without a map of the forest to rely on. Bera says skipping the cloud matters because a drone banking hard around a thin branch can't afford to wait on a server somewhere.
The person also keeps disappearing behind trunks, of course. For that, Bera's post lists an occlusion prediction step. It has the drone guess where its target is headed until they come back into view.
Navigating without GPS is also exactly the kind of autonomy the US military has been pouring money into. Last November, Purdue announced that the Army Research Laboratory had signed a five-year, $1.5 million deal with Bera's lab to build drones and ground robots that can find their way through hostile terrain without satellites. That said, the LinkedIn post doesn't say whether that money paid for the forest flights.

articles.title: Airbnb Cuts Recommendation Staleness from 2 Days to Seconds with Chronon

Airbnb has extended its open source Chronon feature platform with Push Mode and Near Real Time (NRT) Model Transform to update sequence based recommendation embeddings within seconds of guest activity. The change reduced embedding staleness from nearly two days to less than a minute, with typical updates arriving within 10 to 30 seconds. Airbnb also reported a 1.67% improvement in offline NDCG and an approximately 0.33% increase in uncancelled bookings in online A/B testing.
The work builds on Airbnb’s JourneyFormer based sequence recommender, which uses a Transformer encoder to represent a guest’s booking, review and browsing history. Previously, the encoder ran as a daily batch job, generating embeddings that were stored in a low latency store. During a search, the ranking system retrieved the latest embedding and combined it with the live query, keeping the Transformer outside the latency sensitive serving path. However, activity occurring after the daily batch could remain absent from the embedding until the following run, with processing delays bringing effective staleness close to two days.

articles.title: 12 minutos: ese es el tiempo que necesitaría China para transmitir todo el conocimiento de la humanidad de 2007 utilizando esta fibra óptica de alta tecnología

China acaba de anunciar algo difícil de imaginar hace unos años: una velocidad de transmisión de datos de 3,2 petabits por segundo a través de una sola fibra óptica. Para entender la magnitud del experimento basta con una comparación. En 2007, la humanidad disponía de capacidad tecnológica para almacenar unos 295 exabytes de información, una cantidad equivalente a 315 veces el número estimado de granos de arena de la Tierra. Con la velocidad alcanzada por los investigadores chinos, transmitir ese volumen de datos requeriría minutos.
Una humanidad entera en 12 minutos. Ocurrió el pasado 26 de octubre de 2026, cuando el grupo público China Information and Communication Technologies (CICT), con sede en Wuhan, anunció que sus investigadores habían conseguido transmitir 3,2 petabits de información por segundo a través de una fibra óptica experimental.
La velocidad equivale a 400 terabytes por segundo, suficiente, por ejemplo, para transferir más de 20.000 películas en resolución 4K en un solo segundo, según las estimaciones del equipo. También representa una capacidad equivalente a 3,2 millones de conexiones domésticas de 1 Gb/s funcionando simultáneamente. El resultado supera en un 28% los 2,5 petabits por segundo alcanzados por el mismo grupo de investigadores meses antes.

La Police nationale a alerté ce jeudi 29 octobre 2026 sur une campagne de faux courriers envoyés au nom de la Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), qui ciblent les détenteurs de cryptomonnaies.
La lettre, qui reprend tous les codes d’un document administratif, se présente comme une « mise en demeure » liée aux obligations déclaratives sur les actifs numériques.

Un QR code qui mène vers un domaine frauduleux
Le QR code renvoie vers reglement2026.com, un nom de domaine qui n’a en réalité rien à voir avec l’administration fiscale.
Ce domaine est d’ailleurs déjà référencé comme frauduleux sur VirusTotal, un service qui rassemble les analyses de nombreux éditeurs de sécurité pour évaluer la dangerosité d’un fichier ou d’une adresse web.
Le piège est ensuite assez classique. Les victimes se retrouvent face à une interface reprenant les éléments visuels d’un site de l’État. La cible est alors invitée à saisir ses identifiants fiscaux, puis la phrase de récupération de son portefeuille numérique. articles.title: Sony ISP subsidiary data breach exposes 2.5 million customer records
articles.summary:
Sony Network Communications has confirmed a data breach that compromised approximately 2.5 million records containing current and former customers’ personal information.
A Sony Group Corporation subsidiary, the company provides telecommunications and technology services, acting as an internet service provider (ISP) in Japan.
The breach occurred on October 19 and was detected four days later, when the company shut down the compromised servers and blocked external communication.
In an announcement yesterday, the company said that its So-net member database, supporting its internet access service, was accessed by an unauthorized party.
The investigation confirmed that a total of 2,585,481 customer records had been exposed, including the following types of information:
- Full names
- Phone numbers
- Email addresses
- User IDs
- Dates of birth
- Gender
- Internet Connection IDs
No banking, payment card, or other account details were exposed.
An additional 54,401 email addresses from several email services were also exposed along with account passwords. The company advises users to change their passwords.
In the breakdown of exposed records, Sony Network Communications says there are 2,141,986 So-net entries and 443,495 plala (S Course) records. The latter impacts another internet service provider, NTT Docomo, which contracts Sony Network Communications to provide its Docomo Hikari services.

articles.title: The Complexity Between The Bits
articles.summary:
What biological reasoning can teach us about verifying silicon systems.
By Vidya Chandran Darbari and Ashish Darbari
A recent conversation about carbon intelligence and silicon intelligence stayed with me. What interested me was not which one wins, but the complexity we take on as we ask silicon to sense, interpret, decide and act.
My work as an experimental structural biologist taught me to ask what a structure could explain, and what it could not. Solving a molecular structure was not the same as explaining the behaviour of the system to which it belonged. The next question was always about mechanism: what happens when the parts interact? That question shaped my perspective as a deep generalist in life sciences, connecting molecular mechanisms, biological networks and system behaviour.
Now, as Chief Strategy and Operations Officer at Axiomise, I return to that question in a different setting.
A chip is not a cell. But investigating biological complexity can sharpen how we investigate engineered systems—provided the comparison changes a question we ask, an observation we make or an obligation we verify. Otherwise, it remains an interesting analogy.
In life sciences, a protein interaction map is where questions begin. A connection identifies a possible interaction; it does not establish when that interaction matters. Concentration, localization, binding affinity, feedback and timing influence the outcome.

articles.title: Adobe, Veeam, Juniper Networks Patch Critical Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
Adobe, Veeam, and Juniper Networks have released patches for over three dozen vulnerabilities across their products, including multiple critical-severity code execution flaws.
This week, Adobe fixed 12 vulnerabilities in Campaign Classic, Connect, Creative Cloud, and Substance 3D Painter.
The Campaign Classic update resolves eight critical-severity bugs, including code/command injection, incorrect authorization, and XSS issues.
Successful exploitation could lead to arbitrary code execution, security feature bypass, and privilege escalation, Adobe warns in a priority 2 advisory.
Another critical-severity defect leading to arbitrary code execution was addressed in Adobe Connect for desktop and mobile.
The security updates for Creative Cloud and Substance 3D Painter resolve high- and medium-severity security holes leading to code execution, privilege escalation, and memory leaks.

In Backup for Microsoft 365, Veeam fixed four flaws, including a critical issue that could have allowed attackers to read/write configuration data cross-tenant and achieve remote code execution.
It also resolved a critical-severity bug in Backup & Replication that could have allowed unauthenticated attackers to bypass authorization.

Die Google-Mutter Alphabet hat im dritten Quartal ihren Umsatz zweistellig gesteigert, enttäuschte aber trotzdem die Erwartungen der Anleger. Der Umsatz kletterte um 25 Prozent auf 127,6 Milliarden Dollar, blieb jedoch hinter den Prognosen der Analysten zurück.

Google just handed its rivals the keys to Android
Google is giving coding agents like Anthropic’s Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex deeper access to its Android development tools, including devices, performance profilers and production crash reports; now, agents can now investigate bugs, test changes, and verify their own fixes.

articles.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier AI model that you can't use

Just two weeks after rolling out Gemini 4 Argon, Google has announced Gemini 4 Carbon. Carbon is also apparently twice as likely to generate code that is free of vulnerabilities versus Argon. articles.summary:
A disparada dos preços das memórias flash, impulsionada pela demanda de empresas de inteligência artificial, mudou a relação entre a Apple e seus fornecedores. Após anos pressionando fabricantes por descontos, a empresa enfrenta custos maiores e menor poder de negociação.
Segundo a TechInsights, os preços dessas memórias quintuplicaram no último ano, fortalecendo a posição comercial da Kioxia e de outras fabricantes.
Demanda por IA muda o mercado
Durante anos, a Apple foi a maior compradora mundial de memórias flash, chips usados para armazenar fotos, músicas e aplicativos. Seu volume de compras permitia exigir preços baixos e condições contratuais favoráveis.
Dois anos atrás, a empresa comprava quase o dobro da quantidade adquirida em conjunto por Microsoft, Amazon, Meta e Google, segundo estimativas da TechInsights. Agora, essas quatro empresas compram, juntas, o dobro da participação da Apple no mercado.
Em 2026, Meta, Microsoft e Amazon assinaram contratos de fornecimento de longo prazo com a Kioxia, aceitando preços mais altos. Os acordos também protegem os lucros da fabricante caso o mercado mude.
A memória flash representa uma parcela menor do custo de construção de um data center do que da fabricação de um iPhone. As regras contábeis também permitem distribuir esses custos ao longo de vários anos, o que ajuda a explicar por que as empresas de IA conseguem pagar mais pelos componentes.

articles.title: Elle utilise l’IA pour contester ses impôts : le tribunal la sanctionne avec une amende

Le 4 décembre 2025, Marie-Line X a introduit une requête pour contester un redressement fiscal datant de 2023. Autant dire que cette requête n’a pas été bien reçue. En fait, le tribunal administratif de Rennes (Ille-et-Vilaine) lui a infligé une amende de 500 euros pour recours abusif, comme le rapporte Franceinfo. Parmi tous les éléments qui ont abouti à cette amende, le tribunal a constaté « une requête manifestement écrite à l’aide d’un outil d’intelligence artificielle ».
Une amende de 500 euros pour recours abusif
Pourquoi le tribunal a-t-il infligé à Marie-Line X une amende de 500 euros ? Tout d’abord, la contribuable bretonne avait déjà déposé une requête similaire, qui avait été rejetée. Ensuite, elle a saisi le tribunal administratif de Rennes sans avoir préalablement adressé de réclamation à l’administration fiscale, une démarche obligatoire dans ce type de litige. Marie-Line X assure de son côté être « de bonne foi », avoir « suivi les indications écrites » du Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) et n’avoir « jamais été informée d’une dette en 2023 jusqu’à la notification ». Enfin, et non des moindres, le tribunal a relevé un manque de précision dans ses arguments.
Concernant ce dernier point, le magistrat explique : « les moyens de la requête – laquelle a au demeurant été manifestement écrite à l’aide d’un outil d’intelligence artificielle – ne sont pas assortis des précisions les plus élémentaires permettant au juge d’en apprécier la portée et le bien-fondé »…

articles.title: Police are pulling people over because license plate cameras say their travel patterns look "suspicious"

articles.title: Cisco Open Sources Quarry to Catch AI Agent Attacks Hidden in Harmless Steps
articles.summary:
Detecting an AI agent attack isn’t simply finding multiple small needles scattered in a large haystack; it is recognizing whether and for what purpose the needles are connected.
Traditional security controls evaluate single actions to classify whether an intent is bad or benign. This approach fails on AI agent activity when the bad intent only emerges over a series of benign actions. It only becomes apparent if and when the overall sequence of actions is viewed or actioned.
Fraud detection is an example. A bank analyzes each purchase on its own. That’s largely how traditional security operates. Fraud detection, however, needs to see patterns of apparently benign single purchases across multiple purchases, possibly in multiple locations with unlikely timing (potentially employing agent capability). “Agent security needs the same combination of pattern detection and evidence, applied to the steps an agent takes rather than to purchases,” writes Cisco in announcing the open sourcing of its Project Quarry.
Cisco describes Quarry as a neurosymbolic rule language, combining machine learning judgment with rule-based checks. “It covers single-turn and multi-turn large language model (LLM) conversations, agents, tool use, Model Context Protocol (MCP) interactions, and multimodal inputs.”

articles.title: Datadog Builds a Specialist AI Model for SRE Investigations
articles.summary:
Datadog has released Scout, a model trained to investigate production problems. It runs inside Bits Investigation, the company's AI SRE product, where it can pick up an alert, look through telemetry and suggest what caused the problem. Datadog engineers and a small number of customers are using it in a closed preview.
Most of the work described in the announcement concerns cost. An investigation may require many model calls as Bits tries a query, studies the result and decides what to check next. General-purpose models can do this, but Datadog says the bill makes it difficult to run them against every alert. The authors of the announcement want Bits to begin work while an engineer is still responding to the page.
"Our goal is for Bits to serve as an always-on first responder, gathering evidence and identifying likely causes before an engineer steps in."
Othmane Abou-Amal, Ben Cohen, Afshin Rostamizadeh, Ameet Talwalkar, Omri Sass and Daniel Shan
On Datadog's AlertEval benchmark, Scout medium received a similar score to GPT-6.1 Sol high and Claude Opus 5.5 high. Its estimated inference cost was between three and eight times lower. A new study has shown that your smart TV might be tracking you and what you watch, even when you opt out of tracking.
The study, named Watching the Watchers, was conducted by researchers affiliated with Northeastern University in Boston, Massachusetts.
- Essentially, it examines automatic content recognition (ACR) features, which the study noted are built into most available smart TVs—and whether turning ACR off actually stops TVs from sending whatever is on your screen to providers.
The researchers tested TVs running Tizen OS (Samsung), Roku OS (Roku, TCL), webOS (LG), SmartCast OS (Vizio), Google TV OS (Sony, Hisense, TCL), Fire TV OS, and others like VIDAA and Xumo.
To add some context, here is how ACR works: essentially, the TV takes short audio or video snapshots of what is on screen, and those snapshots (or the digital fingerprints made from them) are then sent to the internet or ACR provider. From there, the provider compares what was sent to a library of known content to determine exactly what you are watching. The data can reveal your viewing habits and can be used for targeted ads or sold to other companies.
Interestingly, the researchers found out that antenna broadcasts were almost always tracked on every analyzed system. On the streaming side, no TV tracked YouTube or Netflix, but free ad-supported streaming platform Tubi was tracked on Tizen OS, Google TV on Sony, and VIDAA OS.

articles.title: This open-source keyboard lets you snap keys together in any layout
articles.summary:
The takeaway: Custom keyboard builders can swap out switches, keycaps, plates, and firmware these days, but the layout is usually locked in once the PCB is made. Now, a new open-source project called Keybytes is trying to get around that limitation by giving each key its own tiny circuit board and microcontroller. The keys snap together with magnets and connect to a small hub, allowing a keyboard to start out as a single key and grow into pretty much any shape.
The project comes from Nathan Alspaugh, an MIT freshman studying aerospace engineering, who said he has spent around 100 hours working on it since March. When he posted the project to Hacker News this week, he said the idea came from his frustration that nobody sold triangle- or circle-shaped keyboards.
Each key, called a Keybit, consists of a 19.05mm-square circuit board fitted with a Cherry MX switch and an inexpensive CH32V003 RISC-V chip. The neighboring module, whether another key or the hub, receives power and I2C data through spring-loaded pogo pins along all four edges.
The hub, called the Keyword, occupies the same 1u footprint but stacks two PCBs. An STM32WB55 on the upper board handles Bluetooth and stores firmware for every key. Meanwhile, the lower board houses the charging circuitry for an optional LiPo battery and the USB-C port.
Rather than sharing a single bus, each Keybit bit-bangs a separate I2C connection along each of its four sides. Alspaugh explained in the Hacker News thread that this approach r…

articles.title: Police seize Virtualine bulletproof service tied to ransowmare, cybercrime
articles.summary:
U.S. law enforcement has seized the primary domain of Virtualine, a bulletproof hosting service advertised on cybercrime forums for facilitating illegal activities.
The service also operated under the names Secury, Massgod, Spamhouse, Lanedo, and Omegatech, and promised to shield customers from legal complaints and requests from law enforcement and other authorities.
The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) confirmed that Virtualine marketed services that permitted “illegal/black hat activities” ranging from phishing, spamming, and carding to port scanning.

articles.title: Auto-Generation Of Properties: Methodology Insertion
articles.summary:
Technology is only useful if it improves an existing methodology. Property generation is still refining that goal, but in the long term it could be very useful.
Key Takeaways:
A top-down semiconductor development flow has long been a goal for chip design, and shift left is certainly making that increasingly possible. The problem is that the starting point — the specification — is often incomplete or nonexistent, because the chip industry has been notoriously bad at writing specifications.
There are several ways to insert AI into existing flows. But just because something can be done doesn’t mean it should be. This is one of the big challenges facing AI adoption. Many existing tasks could be done more efficiently using an agentic flow, but it’s not clear whether that is the right thing to do.
This limitation becomes especially apparent when AI starts to help with something that has been woefully inadequate in the past — the creation of good, complete specifications. The big question is whether AI can enable designs, or verification environments, to be automatically derived from a specification. Perhaps a more correct goal is whether AI can help create better specifications. With better specifications, downstream design becomes a lot easier.

A handful of non-NASA missions bound for space stations remain on the spacecraft’s manifest, but all are likely to carry at least one government astronaut. Then Dragon will be retired. The 5 essential layers of AI agent sandboxing on Kubernetes
An AI agent given autonomy to run code will inevitably run code no human has reviewed. It may install model-selected packages, run scripts generated moments earlier, and iterate until a developer’s test passes; that risk is limited to a laptop. For a company, it can extend beyond the agent’s workload to any workload deployed on shared Kubernetes infrastructure. Cluster configurations can limit a container’s system calls, but an allowed call that reaches a kernel vulnerability can still expose the underlying node.
As agents proliferate, this gap has shifted workload isolation from a niche hardening requirement to a baseline need for platforms that run agents. This is a challenge our users at Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) have asked us to help solve.

As expected in the cloud-native space, the community has developed solutions. These solutions exist across five layers: from the pod request, down to the node, and back up to the agent’s session. Platform teams can assemble the stack rather than reinvent it, while native provider support simplifies configuration and maintenance. Managed Kubernetes services offer sandboxed pods this way, but runtimes isolate agentic workloads differently.

Cómo hemos llegado hasta aquí. Empecemos con un resumen breve:
- 2022: entran en servicio los primeros centros de AWS en Aragón.
- 2023: el Gobierno aragonés modifica el PIGA para ampliar su capacidad energética.
- Finales de 2024: AWS pide modificar su evaluación ambiental simplificada.
- Enero de 2026: Ecologistas en Acción anuncia un contencioso contra el PIGA.

In a finding that perfectly sums up the blind faith so many executives have in AI, 77% of board members expect the technology will deliver value in the form of productivity and cost savings. This is despite 97% of organizations being unable to achieve cost savings through productivity alone.
CV Viverito, senior director analyst for Gartner's HR practice, said that organizations will not generate cost savings from AI at this point. Another entirely unsurprising finding is that almost four in ten companies are now over budget on their AI spending.
