Ransomware attacks have become one of the most widespread cybersecurity threats globally, targeting both individuals and organizations. While many users may view ransomware as a personal issue affecting only individual devices, the reality is far more complex. The consequences of a ransomware attack on a home PC can be severe, but when the same attack hits a work laptop, the stakes rise dramatically, impacting not just the user but entire organizations and their stakeholders.
Ransomware typically involves malicious software encrypting files on a device, making them inaccessible until a ransom is paid. However, the impact varies greatly depending on the environment. The difference between a home PC and a work laptop is not only ownership but also the scope and scale of the damage that can follow. Understanding these distinctions is critical for effective prevention and response strategies.
The Home PC Scenario: Personal Data at Risk
When ransomware strikes a home PC, the primary victims are the individual user and their personal data. Photos, documents, and other files can be locked away, causing frustration and potential loss of irreplaceable memories or essential information. The financial impact is often limited to the ransom demand and possible costs for recovery software or professional help, but the emotional and practical toll can be significant.

articles.title: The touchscreen MacBook Pro uses a 'Tandem OLED' panel — so why is its 'PROLED XDR' display different to the iPad Pro's 'Ultra Retina XDR' Tandem OLED panel? Let's dig into the specs
articles.summary:
What's the tech inside the touchscreen MacBook Pro's 'PROLED XDR' screen? Here's why the 'tandem' OLED panel is important
The first OLED MacBook Pro screen has a weird name — here's what's behind it
Apple has unveiled its first OLED MacBook Pro laptops, and that means we've got a new bit of display branding: PROLED XDR. You can have the laptop in 14-inch or 16-inch variants, pre-orders are open now for shipping on or after the 6th of November — and we've gone hands-on with them. Literally, because they're also the first touchscreen Macs.
The name 'PROLED XDR' is a new piece of jargon that Apple's debuting with this machine. So what actually is it?
The short answer is that it's a 'Tandem OLED' panel, which means that it uses multiple layers of organic light-emitting diodes — in this case, two layers. Two OLED layers are better than one because the result is considerably brighter than a single-layer OLED: you literally have two OLEDs firing per pixel. It also boosts longevity, because each of the two layers doesn't have to work as hard, so they have a longer lifespan and are more likely to avoid burn-in.
Apple has stayed away from OLED for its MacBook Pro displays in the past, and clearly that's changed. According to Apple that's because PROLED XDR "finally" overcomes the traditional limitations of OLED: low and variable brightness, off-axis color shift and the risk of burn-in from displaying the same interface elements, such as toolbars and palettes, whenever the screen is on.…

El clip se inicia con un perro haciendo caca en la playa de Vice City y con su dueño recogiéndola y siguiendo su camino. Google to launch secure multi-party computing service for crypto wallets
Google LLC’s cloud unit is preparing to launch a service designed to help financial institutions secure clients’ digital assets.

It’s currently being tested by a group of early adopters described as major financial sector players. Additionally, Google parent Alphabet Inc. is using it to secure its Ethereum and Solana holdings.
Cryptocurrency holders keep their assets in applications called crypto wallets. Every wallet is protected by a unique private key, a snippet of data with a role analogous to a password. Hackers who obtain a wallet’s private key can steal its contents with relative ease.
Google’s Multi-Party Compute service improves the security of crypto wallets by making their private keys harder to steal. It achieves that using an approach called multi-party computation, or MPC.
A wallet’s private key is usually stored on a single device. If hackers compromise that device, they can access its private key. MPC mitigates that attack vector by splitting keys into multiple fragments and storing each one on a separate system. The more devices hackers must breach to steal a key, the less feasible it becomes to do so.
Different MPC services split keys in different ways. Some represent each key fragment as a point on a curved line. When a user needs to make a transaction, the key is mat…

articles.title: Why Kubernetes platforms keep rebuilding a layer they could share
articles.summary:
Why Kubernetes platforms keep rebuilding a layer they could share
Ask a platform team what they built last year, and the list likely includes a Kubernetes controller that creates a few objects in order and copies fields between them. No business logic, just wiring. A Deployment, a Service in front of it, and a ConfigMap whose one interesting value is the hostname the Service reports in its status. Kubebuilder turns building the first controller into a pleasant afternoon. The tenth brings its own reconcile bugs, upgrade path, and on-call rotation. It’s the same controller. It’s slightly different each time, and it exists in thousands of organizations.
Every ingredient, no recipe
Kubernetes has the ingredients: CRDs define new types. Controllers give them behavior. Server-side apply tracks who owns each field. CEL evaluates expressions, and OpenAPI schemas type every field. What Kubernetes does not provide is the recipe. Nothing says that several resources form one thing, or that a value in one comes from the status of another and must wait for it.

There are four different SKUs for the device: the M5 Pro with a 16-core GPU, the M5 Pro with a 20-core GPU, the M5 Max with a 32-core GPU and the M5 Max with a 40-core GPU.
The two M5 Pros start at 1TB SSD with max storage at 4TB; the M5 Max starts at 2TB with max storage at 16TB.
Of course, all the hype is around the 14.2-inch tandem OLED display with a 3024 x 1986 resolution at 254 pixels per inch. Because of the XDR, you can get a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and XDR brightness up to 1000 nits sustained or 2,00o nits peak for HDR content only.
The display can drop as low as 10Hz and go as high as 120Hz with multi-touch gesture support. The M5 Pro has up to 22 hours of video streaming, while the M5 Max has 20 hours of video streaming, both on a 72.6-watt-hour battery. It has three Thunderbolt 5 USB ports, an SDXC card slot, an HDMI port, MagSafe 3 and a 3.5 mm headphone jack.

The rule does not change the regulatory status of the peptide; instead, it states the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will no longer take enforcement action against compounding pharmacies for making the peptides, essentially giving them a green light to freely produce and sell them. Why native PC conversions of console games are suddenly everywhere — Reverse Engineer Anything gives AI agents a unified toolkit, and byte-for-byte checks keep hallucinations in line
The stage was set, all that was needed was a push... from an army of bots.
Over the past weeks and months, it's increasingly commonplace to encounter native PC ports of previously console-exclusive video games, developed with the help of frontier AI models and a new tool named Reverse Engineer Anything (REA). With dozens of titles ported to PC over the past few months, the big questions are: why is this now possible, and what changed?
The better-known conversions like Super Mario Galaxy and Modern Warfare 2 use AI agents, but their handlers mostly still had to interpret results and direct each step of the process. That's now much easier with Reverse Engineer Anything. Although it shows up in many conversations, REA doesn't do the heavy lifting by itself. It's actually a mix between a toolkit and agent harness, wiring together previously disparate tools under one ceiling.
REA analyzes and manages collected information tools: binary analyzers, decompilers, metadata tools, firmware images, database readers, and so on end up linked via agents. Those tools are made available to your AI agent of choice, along with skill files with additional instructions.

articles.title: CISA warns of Fragnesia Linux flaw chained in PHP2Shell attacks
articles.summary:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies to patch a high-severity Linux kernel privilege escalation bug that attackers are chaining with the PHP2Shell flaws in the wild.
Tracked as CVE-2026-46300 and known as Fragnesia, this vulnerability stems from a logic bug in the Linux XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem that lets attackers run malicious code with root permissions.
Fragnesia belongs to the Dirty Frag vulnerability class and has a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit that local attackers can use to gain root privileges on major Linux distributions with kernels released before May 13, 2026.
CISA added CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Wednesday and ordered federal agencies to patch their systems by Saturday 10, as mandated by its Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
The cybersecurity agency didn't share details about ongoing Fragnesia attacks, but it noted that threat actors could chain it with two critical PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), collectively tracked as PHP2Shell, to deploy webshells on unpatched systems.
"This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root," CISA said.
Fragnesia and PHP2Shell exploit chain

SaaS major Freshworks has acquired Israel-based AI startup Robusta Dev, an incident intelligence engine that uses AI to investigate technology disruptions, identify root causes, and recommend remediation actions.
In a company blogpost, Freshworks said that this acquisition will strengthen Freshservice's capabilities, which is Freshworks’ IT service management platform, in incident management and IT operations. It bridges the gap between deep diagnostic intelligence, IT service management, and modern incident orchestration.
Nasdaq-listed Freshworks did not disclose the financial details of the deal.
Founded by Natan Yellin and Arik Alon, Robusta has been heavily optimised for large scale production environments. articles.title: 3 Ways AI Agents Already Operate in Your Browser

Which AI agents can act inside your employees' browsers today? If an agent started browsing this morning, would you know it wasn't the employee? Most security teams can't answer those questions yet. That's not a failure of effort. It's a sign of how quickly AI moved from answering questions to taking action.
AI agents now operate browsers inside authenticated applications, and they get there in different ways: debugging interfaces, extensions, agentic browsers, and emerging standards like WebMCP. Each changes what an agent can access, how its actions are attributed, and whether existing controls can see them.
1. Remote Debugging: Applications Controlling the Browser
One way AI agents operate browsers isn't new at all. It's the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
CDP was built to help developers inspect, debug, and automate Chromium-based browsers. It provides programmatic access to navigation, page content, network activity, and user interactions. Tools like Playwright and Puppeteer have used it for years. AI agents use the same approach to navigate websites, extract information, fill forms, and interact with web applications.
The key distinction: automation doesn't have to originate inside the browser. An external application can connect to a browser with debugging enabled and control its tabs. If that browser has authenticated sessions, the automation can use that access.

The Government of Canada has launched the Telecom Competition Roadmap to improve competition and increase the choices for Canadians.
The roadmap outlines actions that the government will implement:
More choice – to increase competition and give consumers more choices, the government will make it easier for competitors to access existing networks and expand their networks.
Better prices- to help Canadians take advantage of more affordable plans, the Canadian government will spotlight competitive offers, make it easier to shop around and switch providers and eliminate unnecessary fees.
High-quality networks – the Canadian Government will make sure consumers benefit from high-quality services across the country, and the government will help companies deploy the latest fibre-optic networks, experiment with new technologies and strengthen access to reliable connectivity in rural and Indigenous communities.

Over time, against long odds, the pair cleared a path for SpaceX to contracts at NASA and the US military. They sued when things did not go their way. They hollered about unfair playing fields. Most importantly, they delivered quality space products to the US government for less.
And so, after a while, SpaceX found El Dorado and a city of contracts.
Then they started winning everything. So much so that the relationship between the customer and contractor began to change. Slowly at first, but ever more quickly, SpaceX went from needing the US government as an indispensable customer to becoming an indispensable contractor for the nation.

No obstante, los ingresos y las ganancias quedaron por debajo de lo que esperaban los analistas, y sus acciones cayeron cerca de 8% en las operaciones posteriores al cierre del 28 de octubre.
La empresa facturó USD 127.580 millones, un 25% más que un año antes, según CNBC. Los analistas consultados por LSEG, una firma de datos financieros, esperaban USD 128.220 millones. Es el ritmo de crecimiento más rápido desde 2021, pero no alcanzó la proyección del mercado.
La ganancia por acción fue de USD 2,12, frente a los USD 2,87 del mismo trimestre de 2025. Con el ajuste que usa Wall Street, CNBC la ubica en USD 2,67, contra los USD 3,02 que esperaban los analistas. La utilidad neta cayó a USD 26.170 millones, desde USD 34.980 millones.
El director ejecutivo, Sundar Pichai, definió el período como un “trimestre sólido” en el comunicado de resultados y afirmó que Gemini es “el producto de más rápido crecimiento en la historia de Google”. También dijo que la empresa va camino de registrar medio billón de dólares en ingresos anuales, según Deadline.

Customers need application and API protection that “keeps pace without adding operational complexity,” according to kp Papamiltiadis, senior vice president of global partnerships at Oracle. He said F5’s application security expertise would come into OCI backed by Oracle’s cloud infrastructure and support.

Understanding the Stakes for Small Businesses
Disasters strike without warning, and for businesses operating with a single server, the impact can be catastrophic. Floods, fires, and blackouts not only threaten physical infrastructure but also jeopardize critical data and operational continuity. According to a report by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), 40% to 60% of small businesses never reopen after a disaster. This alarming statistic highlights the importance of having a robust disaster recovery plan tailored to businesses with limited IT resources.
For small businesses with only one server, the stakes are even higher. Unlike larger companies with distributed systems and multiple data centers, a single-server setup represents a single point of failure. If that server goes down, the entire business can grind to a halt. This makes it critical to understand the risks and prepare accordingly with a comprehensive disaster recovery plan.
Why a Disaster Recovery Plan is Non-Negotiable
At the core of any disaster recovery strategy lies the ability to restore operations swiftly and efficiently. For a business with one server, downtime translates to total business interruption, loss of customer trust, and potential financial ruin. A disaster recovery plan is a documented, structured approach that ensures a business can recover data, maintain continuity, and resume normal operations after an incident.

En quatre mois, les champions chinois de l’IA ont perdu 40 % en Bourse
Pendant que Wall Street se demande quand la bulle de l'IA finira par crever, la Chine connaît déjà la réponse. L'indice qui rassemble ses champions de l'IA et des puces a fondu de 40 % depuis juillet. Les robots humanoïdes et les GPU nationaux qui faisaient rêver les petits porteurs ont perdu la moitié de leur valeur. Et le plan de Pékin pour drainer l'épargne des ménages vers la tech vacille.
L’agence Reuters a tranché le 26 octobre : en Chine, la bulle de l’IA a déjà éclaté.
Le STAR50, l’indice boursier qui rassemble les champions chinois de l’IA et des puces, a perdu environ 40 % de sa valeur en moins de quatre mois. Près de 480 milliards de dollars se sont envolés, et la chute dépasse largement la tech : les grandes entreprises du pays, toutes activités confondues, ont reculé de 20 % depuis juin.
Aux États-Unis, la Bourse des valeurs technologiques n’a cédé que 6 % depuis son record d’il y a trois semaines. Une égratignure en comparaison. Reuters y voit malgré tout un mauvais présage pour les marchés mondiaux, déjà fébriles.
	
La Bourse s'est ensuite muée en marché haussier spéculatif et débridé. Et maintenant, on voit la bulle éclater.

articles.title: Massive leak exposes 41,000 DHS workers and undercover ICE agents
articles.summary:
An unprecedented leak of Department of Homeland Security records has exposed details of more than 41,000 employees or contractors who work for the department and its constituent agencies. The records include email addresses, phone numbers, and office addresses, but also references to internal systems and sensitive information on undercover and surveillance programs. In all, the leak provides a map of how DHS is organized and how it operates.
The records, which span DHS itself as well as seven component agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement and US Customs and Border Protection, were last updated on August 19, 2026. The transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets and cybersecurity researcher and journalist maia arson crimew previewed the data for WIRED, which they say they obtained from a group calling itself the Department of Peace.
DDoSecrets published the archive, which it calls “Icepick,” on Wednesday. In a press release, DDoSecrets says the data is from DHS’s Okta login system. In a note with the files, the hackers wrote, “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs.”
An Okta spokesperson tells WIRED that it is unaware of any breach of its systems. “We are aware of this report. Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised,” the spokesperson says.

Valve Won't "Be Gatekeepers" by Banning AI Games, As "AI Slop" Complaints Grow
Valve has a growing AI problem on its storefront, and it's not only that game developers are using AI, which is a point of contention for many gamers but not necessarily the biggest concern for developers. Instead, game developers are increasingly reporting that their games are being cloned by developers using AI to clone games from short demos or PR materials ahead of the original game's launch. There has also been an outcry over the number of low-effort AI-generated or AI-assisted games bringing down the overall quality of Steam Next Fest. As reported by Inven, during a recent panel at the Steam Indie Connect developer event, Valve's Tom Giardino and Marc Wilkinson addressed some of these concerns by developers.

articles.title: Cuánto vale el Nokia 1100 hoy y cuánto costaba cuando salió al mercado

El Nokia 1100, presentado en 2003 con un precio aproximado de 100 dólares, se convirtió con el tiempo en el teléfono móvil más vendido de la historia: comercializó 250 millones de unidades en seis años, según un estudio de Visual Capitalist basado en datos de Yahoo Finance y Omdia. Más de dos décadas después, conseguir una unidad original ya no es sencillo, y quienes lo buscan deben recurrir al mercado de segunda mano, donde los precios varían según el estado del equipo.
En plataformas como eBay, los vendedores ofrecen ejemplares usados por montos que fluctúan entre 25 y 70 dólares, dependiendo de la fecha de consulta y la condición del aparato. A comienzos de 2026, algunas publicaciones ubicaban el piso de precio en 70 dólares. Para septiembre del mismo año, el rango había descendido a entre 25 y 40 dólares. La diferencia refleja la dinámica propia de un mercado de segunda mano, donde la oferta disponible y el estado de conservación de cada unidad inciden de forma directa en el valor final.
Un diseño pensado para resistir
El Nokia 1100 se concibió con un enfoque centrado en la funcionalidad y la resistencia, no en la conectividad. Su carcasa robusta, con bordes antideslizantes, y un teclado protegido por una alfombrilla de silicona le permitieron soportar el uso cotidiano en condiciones que hubieran dañado a otros equipos de la época. Discover seven things emotionally intelligent people do differently to manage emotions, communicate better, and build healthier relationships.
Emotional intelligence is not about staying calm all the time or knowing exactly what to say in every situation. It is about understanding your emotions, recognising how others feel, and choosing how to respond rather than reacting impulsively.
In everyday life, emotional intelligence can influence how we handle disagreements, build relationships, respond to criticism, and navigate difficult situations. People who develop this skill are often better equipped to communicate clearly, understand different perspectives, and manage their emotions constructively.
The good news is that emotional intelligence is not simply something you are born with. Many of its essential skills can be practised and strengthened over time.

When someone criticises them, disagrees with them, or says something hurtful, emotionally intelligent people try not to respond immediately out of anger.
They understand that an emotional reaction can sometimes make a difficult situation worse. Instead of sending an impulsive message or saying something they might regret, they give themselves time to process what happened.

A recent poll of the US workforce found that employee engagement in Q3 fell to its lowest level since 2011. Much of the decline came from remote and hybrid employees across the country, especially those in organizations that have adopted AI.
Gallup began tracking employee engagement in 2000, when 26% of employees in the US said they were engaged. That figure stayed steady between 26% and 30% through 2013, then climbed to a peak of 36% in 2020.
But engagement has fallen since the start of the decade. It stood at 29% last quarter, the lowest level in 15 years. It's also two percentage points lower than the previous quarter.
Gallup writes that each percentage point in engagement represents approximately 1.6 million US employees. The Q3 decline is equivalent to about 3.2 million fewer engaged workers, bringing the total decrease since 2020 to approximately 11 million.
The decline reflected two aspects of employees' work experience: knowing what is expected of them and feeling cared about as a person.
Gallup says businesses should care more about their employees' morale, as disengaged workers can impact a firm's productivity, customer service, quality, safety and profitability.

Big quote: Amazon is telling its engineering teams to judge AI coding tools by the software they help deliver, not the volume of tokens they consume. The updated engineering guidelines warn against treating AI adoption, token consumption, code changes and code reviews as performance targets. "We believe that it is best to measure, and be measured by, long-term outcomes," Amazon wrote.
Amazon is not abandoning usage data. It is asking managers to examine those figures alongside other indicators.
The company recommends examining teams at both ends of AI adoption. Low usage may suggest engineers are missing opportunities to improve their work. Heavy usage should prompt a different question: whether delivery is improving enough to justify it. Neither figure settles the question on its own.
The guidance targets tokenmaxxing – deliberately inflating AI consumption to appear productive on internal dashboards.
Earlier this year, Amazon employees were using MeshClaw, an internal AI agent that can deploy code and interact with Slack, to increase their token counts. Amazon shut down an internal leaderboard in May after employees gamed the rankings. Amazon says it has not imposed employee token caps.
Amazon's guidance leaves room for engineers to conclude that a particular task does not benefit from the available tools. It describes that conclusion as "a finding, not a failing," treating an explanation of a tool's limitations as evidence of judgment rather than resistance to adoption.

Why make AI do the talking when it can do the work too? At TechSparks 2026, Google Cloud’s Rajesh Shivani showed how Gemini agents can talk, code and crunch data.
Imagine handing AI 80,000 files and getting back a presentation with charts, images and a clear narrative. Or asking it to build a detailed 3D scene using code, without dedicated rendering software. These are examples of AI moving beyond answering prompts to taking on complex tasks.
At TechSparks 2026, Rajesh Shivani, Head of AI Customer Engineering for Digital Natives, Startups and ITES at Google Cloud, demonstrated how Gemini is being used across voice AI, autonomous agents and software development.

From chatbots to autonomous coworkers

“An agent is nothing now but a model plus a harness,” Rajesh said, describing the infrastructure around a model that manages memory, context, permissions and task execution.

Sous chaque interrupteur de Keybytes se cache un minuscule processeur, et son jeune créateur, étudiant au MIT, a publié l'intégralité des plans en accès libre. Ce rêve de clavier sur mesure a toutefois un prix, et il pique.
Nathan Alspaugh est étudiant en première année d'ingénierie aérospatiale au Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). Fin octobre, il a dévoilé sur GitHub les plans de Keybytes, un clavier mécanique intégralement modulaire. Chaque touche forme un module autonome de 19,05 mm de côté, la taille standard d'une touche, avec son propre microcontrôleur, et s'aimante à ses voisines. Le nombre de touches comme leur agencement relèvent du seul choix de l'assembleur.
L'idée de bâtir un clavier comme un jeu de construction n'est pas (tout à fait) neuve : le MelGeek Pixel accueillait déjà des briques Lego sur sa coque. Keybytes pousse le principe jusqu'à l'électronique elle-même.
	
Il y a quelque temps, en cherchant un clavier à acheter, j'étais frustré de constater qu'il n'existait aucun modèle en forme de triangle ou de cercle.

articles.summary:
Un estudio de HypeAuditor reveló que uno de cada 12 influencers latinoamericanos cuenta con al menos el 50% de su audiencia clasificada como sospechosa. El análisis abarcó aproximadamente 2.9 millones de cuentas públicas de la región en Instagram, sin incluir perfiles de marcas, y con un mínimo de 1.000 seguidores cada una.
La investigación distingue el nivel de riesgo según el tamaño de la comunidad de cada creador. Entre los microinfluencers, con un rango de 10.000 a 50.000 seguidores, el 8.8% de los perfiles presenta esta proporción elevada de audiencia sospechosa. Entre los nanoinfluencers, con entre 1.000 y 10.000 seguidores, la cifra se ubica en 8.2%. En contraste, entre los creadores con más de un millón de seguidores, la proporción cae a apenas el 0.7%.

Crux Labs, an artificial intelligence platform turning enterprise judgment into continuous agent improvement, launched today with over $6 million in funding.
Benchstrength and Misneach led the round, with participation from Analog Ventures and Pareto Holdings.
The scale of enterprise AI agents in deployment can range from thousands to millions of user interactions per day. Existing observability platforms make agentic traces easier for humans to monitor and inspect, but make it difficult to improve agent behavior at higher volumes.
Many teams end up sampling the top 1% or less of traces for manual review based on a particular metric, threshold or random selection, meaning that the vast majority of agent failures pass by.
“Aligning AI agents to human judgment is one of the biggest challenges of our time,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Julie Kheyfets (pictured, left). “Agents are incredible at attaining goals, but they lack access to the years of heuristics that we as humans have collected in our heads.”
From the company’s point of view, if “what good looks like” exists in the heads of experts, chances are that fixes will always arrive late. This could mean weeks passing between a problem appearing as a small glitch and escalating to the point where a ticket is entered into the system and a patch eventually applied. Security ratings company SecurityScorecard Inc. today released an open benchmark for testing whether artificial intelligence models can handle third-party risk management work without being turned against the companies using them.
The TPRM Benchmark is built for vendor risk programs, where a model may need to interpret security telemetry and decide which exposures matter. A lot of what the model reads comes from questionnaires and documents that vendors filled out themselves, and parts of that may be incomplete or manipulated on purpose. SecurityScorecard says generic benchmarks built around static or academic tasks were not designed with that in mind.
On the capability side, tasks cover disciplines such as exposure triage and fourth-party technology risk, and each one starts as a snapshot of SecurityScorecard’s own vendor-risk telemetry that domain experts check before any model is scored. The answer keys are protected. Inputs rotate too, so a model that memorizes the test has less to gain.
Scores are measured against a baseline with confidence intervals attached, and each model gets an autonomy readiness level from L0 to L4 based on its performance across repeated trials. SecurityScorecard says the rating is meant to show how far a model can be trusted to work without human oversight.

articles.title: How AI Redefines Semiconductor Manufacturing, From Materials Up - EE Times

Demand for more powerful AI chips is pushing semiconductor design forward, but commercializing those designs depends on whether chip manufacturing and packaging technologies can keep up.
A far less visible part of the semiconductor ecosystem is therefore coming into focus: the equipment, components, and materials used to manufacture and package advanced chips. As semiconductor processes become more precise and performance requirements rise, materials must operate reliably under more demanding conditions. Materials engineering helps bridge the gap between advanced chip designs and what manufacturers can produce reliably at scale.
Advanced chips raise the bar for materials
Semiconductor manufacturing already requires materials that perform in highly specialized environments. Components used in semiconductor processing equipment must withstand extreme operating conditions, resist mechanical wear, and maintain process stability and precision.
Producing higher-performance devices requires even greater precision in all phases of manufacturing. Even small changes in a component’s dimensions, surface condition, or performance can impair precise semiconductor manufacturing processes. Advanced ceramics can help equipment maintain tight tolerances and consistent performance.

articles.title: ShinyHunters-Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Turns Out to Be Three Chained Flaws
articles.summary:
The critical Oracle PeopleSoft bug that ShinyHunters has exploited since May is not one flaw but three chained together, the researchers who reported it said this week.
Oracle patched all three under a single identifier, CVE-2026-35273, in June. Its root is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) that reaches an internal management interface because PeopleSoft trusts its own loopback address by default, opening the door to remote code execution without a login.
The breakdown comes from Bobby Gould of the Zero Day Initiative (ZDI), whose team reported the flaw to Oracle.
In its analysis, ZDI said it reported three distinct vulnerabilities across two PeopleSoft components, and that it is working with Oracle to assign a separate CVE to each. As of this week, the one June identifier is still the only one on the record.
CVE-2026-35273 affects PeopleSoft Enterprise PeopleTools versions 8.61 and 8.62, carries a CVSS score of 9.8, and lets an unauthenticated attacker take over the server over the network. Oracle released its fix in an out-of-band security alert on June 10. The flaw is on CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
Attackers were already using it before that fix was in place. Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) attribute a campaign to the group it tracks as UNC6240, better known as ShinyHunters, that exploited the flaw between May 27 and June 9, mostly against universities. articles.title: How Edge AI Helps Humanoid Robots React Faster Than a Central GPU - EE Times
articles.summary:
STMicroelectronics argued that humanoid robots should use onboard sensors and cameras to handle fast reactions on the robot, and leave only whole-body coordination to a central GPU, because a round trip to the GPU adds latency a moving robot cannot afford. The chipmaker is still weighing whether to build more powerful MCUs or MPUs for the task, a decision it says depends on how the robotics market develops.
“Every millisecond counts,” Allan Lagasca, director of STMicroelectronics’ robotics segment strategic program, told EE Times. “If you want a fast reaction, you should move the processing to the edge. If you want the entire system to work together, that is where the GPU comes in.”
Running inference closer to the task can reduce the workload sent to a central GPU and avoid delays associated with transferring data and returning commands, Lagasca said. In robotics, those delays can affect physical movement.
When two hands coordinate to transfer an object, for example, a delayed command can cause a joint to miss its target. Even if individual joints miss their targets by only a few millimeters, the combined movement can be affected.
“If inference is performed at the edge, the system can send the necessary command locally and respond faster,” he said.

Tailscale has released version 1.104.4 to fix flaws in its built-in SSH server that could let an attacker reach services and files on other servers that only the root user should be able to touch.
The flaws are in how Tailscale SSH forwards network connections, a job the Tailscale background process carries out with root privileges. To use them, an attacker must already control a device that the network's access rules permit to open an SSH session to the target, with forwarding allowed in that rule.
The flaws come from a report called Tailworm, published days before the fix by Erica Windisch of Cyberdione Labs, who tested released versions of the Tailscale client and the self-hosted headscale control server in a lab.
Tailscale SSH decides who can connect using a device's identity and the network's policy file, not a password or key, so an attacker does not need stolen credentials, only a foothold on a device the policy already trusts.
The flaws "don't allow an unauthenticated attacker to connect to arbitrary Tailscale SSH servers," Tailscale said, and an attacker can still reach only the machines the policy file already allows.
Tailscale SSH's server runs only on Linux and the open-source macOS build; the attacker's own device can be any platform.

articles.title: Fake PS5 emulators are being used to steal gamers' passwords — two well-known GitHub repos, including popular AnyPS5, get hit, infecting gamers' computers with password-scraping malware
articles.summary:
Fake PS5 emulators are being used to steal gamers' passwords — two well-known GitHub repos, including popular AnyPS5, get hit, infecting gamers' computers with password-scraping malware
Emulators downloaded via GitHub may be stealing your passwords, with two well-known projects being exploited.
Malicious GitHub repositories masquerading as two well-known and legitimate PS5 game emulation tools have been identified as spreading malware that steals gamers' passwords. The malware uses self-signed certificates, created using fake company names and on the same day the malware was built — suggesting that the malware campaign may be automated. Just two minutes after infection, a cleanup script scrubs the affected computer of the malware's files, leaving no trace that it was ever present, according to a report shared with Tom's Hardware by NordVPN's Threat Intelligence research team.
The campaign trades on the back of the popularity of two projects that have become popular within the PS5 emulation community. articles.title: Smarter Power Sequencing with GreenPAK™ - EE Times
articles.summary:
Programmable mixed-signal devices can replace sprawling RC networks and firmware-dependent control with compact, deterministic, and adaptable multi-rail sequencing.
Modern processors, FPGAs, memory modules, sensors, and high-speed interfaces rarely operate from a single supply. Each device may require several voltage rails, and those rails often must rise and fall in a defined order. A core supply may need to stabilize before an I/O rail; a memory rail may need to follow a processor rail; and a reset signal may not be released until every relevant voltage is valid. If that choreography is wrong, the result can be excessive inrush current, back-powering, latch-up, corrupted initialization, or, in some cases, device damage.
Why traditional sequencing becomes difficult
The simplest sequencer uses RC delays and logic gates to shift regulator-enable signals. That approach can be adequate for a small, fixed design, but it becomes unwieldy as rail count and supervision requirements grow. Every added stage introduces more passives, more tolerance stack-up, and more potential failure points. Capacitor and resistor variation, temperature, leakage, and aging can shift the effective delay. A timing change late in development may require component substitutions, schematic edits, new layout work, and another board spin.
A microcontroller offers more flexibility, but it also introduces software into a function that may be required before the main processor is ready. Firmware has to boot, ex…

articles.title: Ojos biónicos: así son los implantes que buscan recuperar la visión y ampliar las capacidades de la vista humana
articles.summary:
Restaurar la vista mediante dispositivos electrónicos ya no pertenece únicamente a la ciencia ficción. Investigadores de distintas partes del mundo desarrollaron ojos biónicos capaces de devolver parte de la visión perdida.
En los próximos años, algunos de estos sistemas podrían ir más allá de los límites del ojo humano al incorporar imágenes térmicas, aumento óptico o visión nocturna, según describe Tim Jackson, profesor de Investigación Retiniana del King’s College London, en The Conversation.
Los esfuerzos por combatir la ceguera con implantes acumulan más de dos décadas de historia y tuvieron como foco principal la retina, la capa de células sensibles a la luz que se encuentra en la parte de atrás del ojo. Cuando esa estructura falla de manera grave, la consecuencia puede ser la pérdida total de la visión.
Dos de los primeros sistemas para revertir ese daño fueron el chip subretiniano de la alemana Retina Implant AG y el Argus II. El primero cerró por falta de progreso médico; el segundo combinaba una cámara con un chip estimulado por 60 electrodos y, pese a la autorización de la Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos (FDA) de Estados Unidos en 2013, tampoco logró resultados sólidos. Ambos fueron abandonados en 2019.
Los primeros implantes ofrecían destellos de luz, no imágenes

articles.title: "Es una cuestión de salud mental": cada vez más padres están pagando hasta 260 euros la noche a niñeras nocturnas
articles.summary:
Blanca Yamira tiene 56 años, trabaja como niñera y cobra alrededor de 260 euros por jornada. Un mes bueno factura más de 4.000. Suena extraño, pero es que Yamira no es una babysitter cualquiera. De hecho, lo que hace ni siquiera encaja del todo en esa etiqueta. Ella no se dedica a cuidar niños que se quedan solos en casa. Su función arranca a las nueve de la noche y se prolonga hasta las siete de la mañana, toda una noche durante la que suple a los padres que acaban de tener un bebé. En otras palabras, cuando el recién nacido llora o se desvela es ella quien lo atiende. Mientras, el padre y la madre siguen durmiendo plácidamente en cama.
Yamira es lo que se conoce como una ‘night nannie’.
Una persona, dos tareas. La historia (y experiencia) de Yamira la conocemos gracias a Corriere della Sera, que hace poco publicó un reportaje sobre ‘niñeras nocturnas’ que trabajan en diferentes ciudades de Italia.
No todas cobran lo mismo ni tienen la misma experiencia, pero por lo general comparten una serie de características: se trata de puericultoras que se desplazan a las viviendas de sus clientes por las noches (habitualmente entre las nueve y las seis o siete de la madrugada) para desempeñar un doble papel. Atienden a los bebés. Y permiten a los padres descansar.
Noches en vela. “Siempre estoy ahí, lista para actuar”, bromea Yamira, que ahora mismo trabaja para una familia de Lugano, en Tesino, al sureste de Suiza. Su turno empieza cuando termina el de la mayoría de niñeras diurnas: …

articles.title: Anthropic's Unreleased AI Model Chains Flaws Into Working Chrome, Safari, Windows and Linux Exploits
articles.summary:
An unreleased Anthropic AI model found security flaws in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux and chained them into working proof-of-concept exploits, the company said in its latest report.
The exploits were built in the lab after the model was prompted, not seen in any real attack, and Anthropic reported every flaw to the vendor first, so all of them are already patched. One proof of concept opened the Calculator app on a stock Mac running Chrome within seconds of a page loading, with no further clicks.
Anthropic's Frontier Red Team described five chains in a research post. The strongest claim is not any single bug, but that one model found several separate flaws and combined them into a working exploit, something the company says has until now been the work of a few specialist teams. That capability claim rests on Anthropic's own account.
The patches and the fact that Apple and Google credit Anthropic and its Claude model for specific fixes can be verified with the vendors.
What a reader cannot check is how much of each chain the model built on its own. Anthropic says the work needed only "initial prompting" and "little human involvement," but it does not break down what a person did at each step, and it does not name the model beyond calling it an unreleased, internal research model.

Fujifilm plans to boost production of magnetic tape by as much as 5x as it works to keep up with demand for the data storage medium that has seen a jump in popularity amid ongoing global AI data center buildouts. The Japanese firm will spend 10 billion yen ($63.3 million) to increase capacity at its Odawara plant throughout its fiscal year 2028. The move will enable it to produce more advanced tapes with capacities of up to 100TB each, Nikkei Asia reports. The expansion of production capacity will mark the company's largest investment in tape-based storage in around 20 years. Fujifilm first began working on magnetic tape technology back in 1954 when it was used for television broadcasting equipment.
Nowadays, magnetic tape is the go-to storage option for data centers everywhere as a form of long-term data backup. While tapes lag behind solid-state drives and traditional spinning hard disks in terms of performance, tapes are hard to beat when it comes to their durability and relatively low cost for storing huge amounts of data. But samples won't land until Q3 2027
- FADU's File-Semantic SSD runs path lookup, permission checks, and file-to-flash mapping in firmware instead of on the host
- NFSv3 requests ride inside standard NVMe commands, so GPUs, DPUs, and remote clients can reach files without requiring a host file system
- Its headline 460,000 ops/s result came from a PCIe 5.0 host, with PCIe 6.0 results promised by Q1 2027
South Korean controller designer FADU has shown off an SSD that understands files rather than just blocks, betting that the next bottleneck in AI storage is not raw bandwidth but the CPU time spent working out where data lives.
The File-Semantic SSD (FS-SSD), unveiled at the OCP Global Summit, moves file lookup, access checks and file-to-address translation into firmware on FADU's sixth-generation controller.
FADU's whitepaper promises GPUs, DPUs and network cards a route to their files with "no host filesystem, no block layer, and no storage-server CPU in the path." Partner samples are not expected until Q3 2027.

Hwang appears to be quite technically proficient and provided a detailed write-up of the situation. articles.title: Critical 16-Year-Old UEFI Flaw Can Run Code Before Secure Boot on Network-Booting Servers
articles.summary:
A critical 16-year-old flaw in EDK II, the open-source code that most hardware makers use to build UEFI firmware, can allow an attacker to run code on a machine before its operating system loads, but only while the machine is booting over the network.
UEFI firmware is the software that runs first when a computer is switched on, before the operating system. An attacker who can reach the machine with a crafted network message during such a network boot can hang the boot, or, with work tailored to the exact firmware build, run their own code before Secure Boot and other startup defenses load.
An attacker needs no password and no existing access to the machine, but does need to reach it over the network during the short window when it is booting this way.
Red Hat and SUSE, which both ship the affected code, rated the flaw as one an attacker exploits from an adjacent network position rather than across the open internet.
TianoCore, the project behind EDK II, published an advisory on October 22 and rated the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, 9.5 out of 10. A code fix exists, but no stable release of EDK II contains it yet, and the advisory still lists no patched version, so most users have nothing to install today.
What the Flaw Lets an Attacker Do
The flaw is a buffer overflow in EDK II's network-boot code, known as PXE. During a PXE boot, a machine loads its startup image from the network instead of from a local disk.
As part of this, the PXE driver listens for ICMP error messages…

Apple bringing back the illuminated logo back is directly attributable to the PROLED XDR display. Each pixel in an OLED panel is emissive, which means there's no need for a backlight. articles.title: Researcher Reveals How Logic Bugs Alone Cracked Microsoft Edge in $175,000 Pwn2Own Win
articles.summary:
A chain of logic flaws, with no memory corruption, can turn a malicious web page into code running on a Windows computer outside Microsoft Edge's sandbox, a security researcher has shown.
Orange Tsai of DEVCORE published the full method on October 28, five months after the chain won $175,000 at the Pwn2Own Berlin contest in May. Microsoft fixed the Edge bugs the day after the contest, so an up-to-date browser is not at risk.
A browser sandbox is the wall that keeps a web page's code inside the browser and off the rest of the computer. Breaking out of it, and then running a program, is what turns a web bug into full control of the machine.
Browser escapes like this almost always rely on memory corruption. This one used none. In his write-up, Tsai describes a chain built solely from logic errors in how Edge and Windows handle ordinary features, and he says the whole exploit is under 100 lines of code.
The result is a universal cross-site scripting (UXSS) primitive: a way to run JavaScript on any website, bypassing the content security policy meant to prevent it.
Because the attack starts from the browser's own process, it can reach sites like google.com that an ordinary web bug cannot touch. Tsai calls this a new attack surface rather than a one-off bug.
This was a competition exploit, not an attack seen in the wild. Tsai demonstrated it on stage at Pwn2Own; there is no evidence it has been used against real users, and the public CVE records list exploitation as none. One step …

Its main purpose is to facilitate critical attack phases like vulnerability exploitation, credential access, data exfiltration, and to maintain continued access to victim environments. The activity stands out for two main reasons -

articles.title: Hackers Exploited Cisco SD-WAN Flaw to Plant Malware Built to Steal Encryption Keys
articles.summary:
Hackers exploited a critical Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN flaw, fixed in February, to plant custom malware inside the systems that control an organization's SD-WAN network.
The malware, called KeyDrift, is designed to copy the keys that encrypt traffic between sites and store them for later use, Cisco Talos said on October 28. Talos calls the attacks historical but does not specify when they occurred or whether any keys were sent.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-20127 and has a CVSS score of 10.0. It allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication and gain administrative privileges on these control systems. On a Controller, the attacker can log in as a high-privileged internal account that is not root.
When Cisco disclosed the flaw in February, Talos tracked its exploitation as UAT-8616, a cluster of activity it said went back to at least 2023.
In Cisco's traditional key exchange, each SD-WAN router periodically generates an AES key for its traffic and sends it to the Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart). The Controller passes the keys on to other routers. A process on the Controller called vdaemon runs the encrypted control connections that carry these keys.
On a compromised Controller, a KeyDrift component called LittleFilch hooks into vdaemon and reads control messages after they are decrypted. For a preset list of edge routers, it pulls out their IP addresses and a 32-byte field. Talos assesses that field as the AES-256 key material that the Controller…

An attacker tried to exploit a critical GitLab vulnerability on the Alpine Linux project's own GitLab server a week after GitLab released a fix, Alpine Linux said on 28 October.
The flaw, CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS score: 10.0), can let an attacker run code on a GitLab server through a crafted regular expression in a CI configuration. Alpine found no evidence that the attack worked but cannot rule it out, so it rebuilt the server from scratch and reset every account's password.
GitLab's fix is a set of patches to the Ruby that GitLab ships in its own packages and container images. Alpine's GitLab image used standard Ruby, so upgrading the server to GitLab 19.3.6 on 22 October did not fix the flaw.
For anyone running GitLab on their own Ruby, built from source or in their own container image, "upgrading GitLab is not enough," Alpine said. Those servers also need Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9 or later, and users of Alpine's alpinelinux/gitlab image need to pull 19.3.6 again.
The server gitlab.alpinelinux.org hosts aports, the repository from which Alpine's packages are built. Packages built from 20 to 24 October, and the 21 October releases, came from aports changes verified against records outside GitLab, according to Alpine.
Those releases include the minirootfs files that the official Alpine Docker images are built from. Alpine is extending the checks to 27 October, when it closed the server. The keys that sign its packages and releases have never been on the GitLab server.

articles.title: 26,400 Valid Cloud and AI Credentials Found Exposed in Public Gitee Repositories
articles.summary:
26,400 credentials that developers left in public code on Gitee, a Chinese code-hosting service, still worked when a researcher tested them. Anyone who copied one from that code could have used it.
Independent researcher Ben Zimmermann found them by scanning 7.25 million public Gitee repositories and reported the results on October 28. Most were keys for cloud and AI services, led by 9,473 Alibaba Cloud AccessKey pairs.
Zimmermann sent the vendors with the most exposed keys a list of their credentials, but he did not contact the developers who leaked them. When he published, he had not confirmed that any of the reported credentials had been revoked. So anyone who has pushed a key to a public Gitee repository cannot assume it has been revoked.
The scan ran for about a month, but Zimmermann did not provide the dates, so it is unclear how long ago the credentials were tested. He also did not say whether anyone else had used them.
He ran two secret scanners, TruffleHog and Kingfisher, over every repository. Both tried each credential against the service that issued it and kept only those that worked, he wrote.
The scanners read each repository's full commit history. A key that a developer later removed from the code could still be found and counted there.
The 26,400 figure counts each credential once, regardless of how many repositories it appeared in. By commit date, 12,242 of the credentials came from 2025, nearly half the total. Some dated to the late 2000s.

A flaw in Telegram for Android allowed an attacker to run code on a victim's phone via a voice call once the victim answered, according to security startup NebuSec.
The attacker needed only an ordinary Telegram account. Telegram fixed the flaw in version 12.10.4 of the app, released in late September, and NebuSec disclosed it on October 29.
The flaw can be triggered in every version from 8.6.2 through 12.10.3, NebuSec's co-founder and chief executive said in an email to The Hacker News. Those versions came out between March 2022 and September 2026.
The company confirmed it in private phone calls on ARM64-based phones and has no evidence so far that it directly affects Telegram's iOS and desktop apps or group calls.
Anyone using Telegram for Android should make sure the app is on version 12.10.4 or later. The version number appears at the bottom of the app's Settings page. The flaw had no CVE identifier as of October 29.
The Hacker News has asked NebuSec and Telegram whether the flaw was used in real attacks, and asked NebuSec what an attacker's code could reach on a phone.
During a Telegram call, the two apps send each other short messages to set up the call and report its state. One type, called MediaState, reports whether the microphone is muted, whether the camera is on, and how the video is rotated.
The flaw was in the code that reads MediaState messages. That code did not handle missing fields correctly and accessed memory it should not, according to NebuSec.

articles.title: Webinar: How to Build AI Threat Readiness Into Your Security Operations
articles.summary:
Security teams have spent years trying to detect threats faster. AI is changing the harder part: how much time defenders have left to act.
Advanced AI models can now help attackers discover vulnerabilities, generate exploit code, and move through weaknesses faster than traditional security processes were built to handle.
The challenge is no longer just finding another vulnerability or generating another alert. It is knowing which exposures matter, what an attacker can reach, and which issues need to be fixed first.
That is the focus of next week's webinar, How to Build AI Threat Readiness Across Your Security Operations, featuring an expert from Wiz. The session will show how security teams can improve visibility, prioritize real risk, and shorten the path from detection to remediation.
Most security teams already have plenty of data. They have vulnerability findings, cloud alerts, identity signals, application telemetry, and threat detections. The harder problem is connecting those signals quickly enough to answer the questions that drive action.
Is this vulnerability reachable? Does the exposed asset contain sensitive data? Can an attacker move from it to something more important? Who owns the affected system? What should be fixed first?
When those answers live across different tools and teams, investigations slow down. That delay matters more when attackers can automate parts of the discovery and exploitation process.

articles.title: Sabotage de câbles sous-marins : pourquoi la Chine inquiète Washington au plus haut point

Un nouveau rapport commandé par le Congrès des États-Unis décrit comment Pékin pourrait couper, discrètement, les câbles sous-marins qui relient les États-Unis à l’Asie. Nouvelle preuve de la nécessité de protéger ces infrastructures critiques.
Ancres traînées sur le fond, filets de chalutiers, glissements de terrain sous-marins… La grande majorité des coupures de câbles sont accidentelles. Mais depuis quelques années, des incidents troublants en mer Baltique comme près de Taïwan, impliquant des navires russes ou chinois, soulèvent de sérieuses questions.
Dans ce contexte, la commission américano-chinoise sur l’économie et la sécurité (USCC), un organe indépendant qui conseille le Congrès américain, a ordonné un rapport visant à réellement évaluer ce dont la Chine serait capable. Sa conclusion : le pays cherche à s’imposer comme la puissance dominante des fonds marins.
Une arme parfaite pour exploiter la « zone grise »
Ainsi, Pékin serait en train de mettre au point des technologies à double usage : un submersible capable de plonger à 10 000 mètres, baptisé Striver, des essaims de drones sous-marins interconnectés et, à l’étude, des coupeurs de câbles « hibernants ». articles.title: Ofcom reveals age-check methods for UK social media ban — facial scans and photo ID spark privacy pushback as 40% of teens plan workarounds
articles.summary:
'The risks aren’t hypothetical': Ofcom reveals age-check plans for UK social media ban — but privacy experts aren't convinced
Take your pick
- Ofcom has assessed the best ways of enforcing age checks online
- The regulator also identifies methods that aren't effective
- Around 4 in 10 under-16s plan to try to get around the ban in the UK
Back in June, the UK government ruled that under-16s should be banned from social media platforms, with enforcement scheduled to start during the first half of 2027. Now the communications regulator Ofcom has set out the ways it expects tech companies to abide by the law.
In its new announcement (via the BBC), Ofcom highlights four "highly effective" methods for keeping under-16s out of apps and off sites they shouldn't be accessing — and they're all going to be familiar to anyone who's used age-gated services online in recent times.
The four methods are photo ID matching (using something like a passport or driving license), bank-based checks (Ofcom says 90% of UK 16-17 year-olds have a bank account), digital ID services (a third-party service like EasyID or Yoti), and facial age estimation via a webcam (which Ofcom says is best deployed as a secondary check).

articles.title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon Leads Benchmarks for Finding, Exploiting, and Patching Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
Google on Wednesday took the wraps off Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities.
"It shows significant gains across coding and agentic tasks as well as across key capabilities critical for cybersecurity defense, landing a firm lead in SEC-bench Pro (88.2%) for finding vulnerabilities, ExploitGym (54.8%) for exploitation, and CWE-bench (71.0%) for patching," Koray Kavukcuoglu, senior vice president of Google DeepMind and chief AI architect at Google, said.
On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index benchmark, Carbon leads with a score of 59, surpassing Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 (58), OpenAI GPT-6 Astra (57), GPT-6.1 Sol (55).
One of the core focus areas is cybersecurity, where the latest iteration reportedly delivers significant performance improvements across the board, including vulnerability detection, validation, and remediation. Carbon is also twice as likely to generate secure code versus Argon.
Google also emphasized that Carbon attempts to respond to complex or high-pressure tasks by seeking human input in the face of ambiguity rather than "guessing or forcing a path forward," as well as resisting every evaluated attack attempt at indirect prompt injection.

articles.title: La Fnac écope de 7 millions d’euros d’amende pour avoir pisté les utilisateurs de son appli
articles.summary:
La CNIL a infligé une amende de 7 millions d’euros à la Fnac pour un traceur intégré à son application mobile. Celui-ci collectait l’historique de navigation des utilisateurs, y compris lorsqu’ils avaient refusé de donner leur consentement.
La Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés (CNIL) a sanctionné deux sociétés du groupe Fnac Darty d’une amende totale de 7 millions d’euros pour non-respect des règles sur les cookies et autres traceurs dans l’application mobile de la Fnac. Le gendarme des données a rendu publique sa décision ce jeudi 29 octobre 2026. En cause, on retrouve un dispositif qui transmettait à un domaine tiers les produits consultés par les utilisateurs, afin d’alimenter des recommandations personnalisées, sans leur consentement. Le régulateur exige désormais une mise en conformité rapide, sous peine d’astreinte.
Dans l'application Fnac, un traceur qui prenait des notes
Tout a commencé avec une plainte de l'association None Of Your Business (NOYB), fondée par le militant autrichien Max Schrems, rompue aux bras de fer avec les géants du numérique. La CNIL a ensuite longuement étudié l'application en mars 2024. Elle a constaté que pendant son utilisation, celle-ci envoyait des requêtes vers un domaine tiers, contenant un identifiant attribué par la Fnac à chaque utilisateur et des informations sur son activité, à commencer par les produits consultés. Le tout sans que l'intéressé ait donné son accord.

articles.title: La FIA mise à fond sur l'IA d'Amazon pour imaginer la F1 de demain
articles.summary:
La FIA a officialisé, mercredi, un partenariat mondial avec Amazon Web Services. Le géant du cloud mettra son intelligence artificielle au service des règlements des futures Formule 1, mais aussi de la pratique amateur.
Déjà partenaires de longue date sur la data notamment, la Fédération automobile internationale (FIA) et Amazon Web Services (AWS) ont annoncé, mercredi, avoir scellé une nouvelle union, plus globale encore, sur l'intelligence artificielle, le cloud, le machine learning et l'infrastructure cloud. Le groupe américain devient le partenaire officiel de l'instance sur toutes ces composantes. Le géant du cloud connaissait déjà bien les paddocks, mais le voilà désormais officiellement associé à ceux qui écrivent les règles. Qu'il s'agisse des souffleries virtuelles, des ingénieurs épaulés par l'IA ou des licences dématérialisées, l'accord va de la F1 aux courses de club, pour concerner autant la monoplace de demain que le pilote amateur du dimanche.

On sait que la FIA fait déjà tourner ses simulations aérodynamiques sur les capacités de calcul haute performance d'AWS. Le principe s'appelle d'ailleurs la simulation numérique des fluides. articles.title: FBI leads action to shut down Virtualine bulletproof service linked to major cybercrime activity
articles.summary:
FBI leads action to shut down Virtualine bulletproof service linked to major cybercrime activity
Virtualine was hosting multiple illegal forums
- FBI and international partners seized infrastructure tied to Virtualine, a hosting provider allegedly serving cybercriminals
- Authorities say the service facilitated phishing, ransomware operations, illicit crypto activity, and other crimes
- Investigators seized servers and customer data, though no arrests have been announced so far
The FBI has announced it seized the website of Virtualine, a bulletproof hosting service that allegedly allowed child pornography, laundered stolen and extorted crypto, and facilitated a wide range of other criminal activities.
The operation was carried out in partnership with German and Dutch authorities, as well as multiple private companies, with police raiding a data center in Limburg to seize “dozens of physical servers” that also hosted “hundreds” of virtual servers. As a result, they gained access to information about more than 3,000 of Virtualine’s customers, it was said.
“The police are currently taking follow-up actions towards these users,” the Dutch police said, although it’s difficult to say how valuable the information will be, since most bulletproof hosting providers don’t ask for private data, and criminals are good at hiding it, as well.
